# reminder-producer implementation plan â€” Round 3 (Claude revision)

Responds to Codex round 2 (6.2/10, `round-2-codex-output.txt`, 13 required changes). Everything
from round 1/2 NOT contradicted here stands unchanged (names in round-1 Â§1, error taxonomy
conclusion that no new `AppError` subclass is needed, most of round-2's port/schema-file-location
corrections). This round's central fix: **the checkpoint-before-continuation ordering bug (required
changes 1+2) is resolved by using this codebase's OWN transactional outbox pattern for the
checkpoint transition** â€” the same mechanism `producer.ts:264-306` already uses for
claimâ†’dispatch, applied one layer up, to scan-pageâ†’continuation. Round 2's own "outbox doesn't
apply here, there's no aggregate write" reasoning (round 1 Â§4) was the actual mistake: **the lease
row IS the aggregate being written at checkpoint time** â€” this was hiding in plain sight.

## Required changes 1+2: checkpoint/continuation â€” outbox-atomic, not send-then-checkpoint

**`SQS_REMINDER_SCAN_CONTINUATION_V1` is reinstated in `OutboxDestination`** (round 2 wrongly
removed it). Checkpoint transition (after a page's candidates are durably published, see Â§7 below)
is now ONE `TransactWriteItems`, same shape as `producer.ts:286-306`:
```ts
const outboxEntries: DynamoTransactPutEntry[] = [];
appendToTransaction(outboxEntries, deps.tableName, continuationEvent, "SQS_REMINDER_SCAN_CONTINUATION_V1");
await deps.store.transactWrite([
  { Update: buildUnscopedVersionedUpdate({ tableName, key: leaseKey, expectedVersion: leaseVersionThisInvocationRead, set: { lastEvaluatedKey: nextKey /* or REMOVE + status: "COMPLETED" on last page */, leaseUntil: now + LEASE_MS, pagesProcessed: pagesProcessed + 1, candidatesPublished: candidatesPublished + thisPageCount }, extraConditions: [{ expression: "ownerToken = :myToken AND #startKeyCond", ... }] }) },
  ...outboxEntries,
]);
```
`DispatchOutboxRelay` (DynamoDB Streams, `producer.ts:270`'s existing mechanism) is extended to
also recognize `SQS_REMINDER_SCAN_CONTINUATION_V1` and publish to the scan queue instead of the
dispatch queue â€” same relay, same sweeper-recovers-publish-failures guarantee, routed by the
existing `destination` discriminator (no new relay Lambda). **Verified this round, not just
asserted**: `src/workers/dispatch-outbox-relay/relay.ts:12-14,22-27,122-152` shows the relay is
ALREADY a generalized multi-destination router (`senders: Record<OutboxDestination, Sender>`,
one sweeper instance covers multiple destinations) â€” it already recognizes
`SQS_REMINDER_DISPATCH_V1` and `SQS_NOTIFICATION_EMAIL_V1` side by side, so adding a third
`senders` entry for `SQS_REMINDER_SCAN_CONTINUATION_V1` (pointing at the scan queue URL) is the
exact, already-precedented extension point â€” no relay redesign needed. **This closes required change 1's
exact failure trace**: a continuation now literally cannot exist in SQS until the checkpoint
transaction has committed, so "successor consumed before predecessor checkpoint" is impossible by
construction â€” there is no window where a successor can arrive early, because the successor's own
existence is downstream of (caused by) the checkpoint, not concurrent with it. Required change 2's
"specify a rigorous successor protocol" is answered by removing the need for one: at-least-once
delivery of the SAME continuation (streams relay redelivery, sweeper retry, or SQS standard-queue
redelivery) is idempotent because the checkpoint that produced it already advanced
`lastEvaluatedKey` â€” a redelivered continuation's handler re-reads the CURRENT lease row, finds
`lastEvaluatedKey` already matches (or is already past) what the message describes as "next to
process," and either does the work once (first delivery) or no-ops (subsequent redeliveries,
detected by comparing the message's OWN `lastEvaluatedKey` against the row's, exactly as round 2
proposed â€” this piece survives unchanged, now sitting on a sound foundation instead of a broken one).

**Cross-tenant envelope** (needed since `DomainEvent.tenantId: string` is non-optional,
`src/shared/contracts/events.ts:24`): continuation events use `tenantId: "SYSTEM"` â€” a documented
sentinel, precedented by this same file's existing `actor: { type: "SYSTEM" }` shape for
system-originated events (no new concept, reuses an existing "not a real tenant" convention this
codebase already has).

## Required change 3: work-unit enumeration â€” matches today's exact loop shape

Round 2 wrongly collapsed to "one message per shard." Corrected: the EventBridge-triggered
invocation reproduces `producer.ts:161-168`'s existing enumeration exactly â€” `lookback` (default 15,
`deps.lookbackMinutes ?? 15`, unchanged constant) inclusive minutes Ã— `activeGenerations(shardConfig,
now)` (unchanged, handles legacy generations already) Ã— that generation's shard partitions
(`gsi3PartitionsForMinute`, unchanged) â€” for EACH resulting (generation, shardId, minute) triple,
attempts a lease acquire and, if it wins (fresh or reclaim), sends ONE start message. A triple
whose lease is already `IN_PROGRESS`-unexpired or `COMPLETED` is skipped (no message sent) â€”
exactly today's implicit "already done" behavior, now explicit. **Lease key now includes
generation**: `PK: SCAN#<shardFnVersion>#<shardId>#<minuteISO>`, `SK: LEASE` â€” collision-free
across reshard generations (round 2's gap, fixed). At `lookback=15` Ã— up to 2 concurrent
generations (a reshard transition window) Ã— 4 shards = up to 120 (generation,shard,minute) triples
evaluated per tick, but the vast majority are cheap `COMPLETED`-skip reads (already-finished older
minutes) â€” only the LATEST 1-2 minutes per (generation,shard) are ever genuinely `IN_PROGRESS`
under normal load, so real concurrent scan work stays bounded near `generations Ã— shards` (â‰¤8), not
120 (this bound feeds Â§8's revised capacity numbers).

## Required change 4: message shapes â€” command-envelope for candidates, new system-envelope only for continuation

**Claim-candidate messages** (`SQS_REMINDER_CLAIM_CANDIDATE_V1`, NOT outbox-routed â€” no aggregate
transaction backs a raw GSI3 row) genuinely have a `tenantId` (parsed from `GSI3SK` before
publishing) and DO fit the existing `command-envelope.v1.json` shape unmodified: `commandType:
"reminder.claim-candidate.v1"`, `tenantId` (real tenant), `deduplicationKey:
"${tenantId}|${occurrenceId}|${pageOwnerToken}"`, `data: { occurrenceKey: {PK,SK}, entityType,
gsi3sk }`. New schema file `schemas/queues/reminder-claim-candidate.v1.json`:
`"allOf": [{ "$ref": "command-envelope.v1.json" }, { "properties": { "data": { "required":
["occurrenceKey","entityType","gsi3sk"], "properties": { "entityType": { "enum":
["ReminderOccurrence","DocumentChasingOccurrence"] }, ... } } } }]` â€” same `allOf` pattern as
`reminder-dispatch.v1.json:6-22` (re-read this round, confirmed shape).

**Scan-continuation messages** genuinely have no real tenant (cross-shard/tenant coordination) â€”
forcing them into `command-envelope.v1.json` (which requires a real `tenantId`) would be a lie, so
a NEW `schemas/queues/system-envelope.v1.json` is added: same shape as `command-envelope.v1.json`
minus the `tenantId` requirement, plus a fixed `"tenantId": { "const": "SYSTEM" }` (kept present,
not dropped, so every queue message in this codebase has the same top-level field set â€” simpler
for any shared tooling that reads `tenantId` generically off an envelope, e.g. log correlation).
`schemas/queues/reminder-scan-continuation.v1.json` uses `allOf: [{"$ref":
"system-envelope.v1.json"}, ...]`, `data: { shardFnVersion, shardId, minute, ownerToken,
lastEvaluatedKey (nullable) }`. Both new schemas get valid+invalid fixtures added to the existing
consolidated `test/contract/schemas.test.ts` (round 2's correction, unchanged).

## Required change 5: sender-fault candidates â€” terminal, not dropped

Reversed from round 2: **any `SenderFault: true` entry in a `SendMessageBatch` response fails the
WHOLE page invocation** (throws after attempting the OTHER entries in that chunk, so
non-sender-fault entries still get their retry chance first) rather than being silently dropped.
This means the checkpoint transaction (Â§1-2) never runs for that page, so no continuation is ever
produced for it â€” the chain is stuck `IN_PROGRESS` until `leaseUntil` expires, at which point the
NEXT eligible tick's reclaim (Â§3) retries the ENTIRE page from the same `lastEvaluatedKey` (safe,
`queryGsi3Page` is a pure read). New metric `CandidateSenderFault` (Count, no dimensions) with an
alarm at >0 over any 5-minute period (fast detection â€” a sender fault means a real bug in candidate
construction, worth paging on immediately rather than waiting for the DLQ-age alarm's 1-hour
threshold). Retryable (non-sender-fault) entries: the ENTIRE original chunk is retried (not just
the failed IDs) using `nextAttemptDelayMs` (`outbox.ts:192-197`, reused as-is â€” same backoff
shape, not reinvented), capped at 3 attempts before the page throws as a transient failure (goes
through normal SQS-level retry of the scan/continuation message itself, `maxReceiveCount=5`).

## Required change 6: capacity â€” worst case is one shard/minute absorbing the full burst, not an even split

Corrected: 10,000 occurrences landing in a SINGLE (shard, minute) â€” not spread across shards â€” is
the real worst case (no proof of uniform hashing exists in this codebase, confirmed by round 2's
own finding; assuming otherwise was round 1/2's error). 10,000 Ã· 200/page = 50 pages, chained
sequentially through outbox-relay hops. Each hop: checkpoint transaction (~50ms) + DynamoDB
Streams propagation to `DispatchOutboxRelay` (typically sub-second, occasionally a few seconds
under load â€” no repo measurement exists, so **2s is used as an explicit conservative per-hop
upper bound**, not a measured average) + SQS send + next invocation's cold/warm start. **50 hops Ã—
~2.5s conservative-worst-case per hop â‰ˆ 125s to fully drain a single-shard 10k burst** â€” stated as
an explicit bound, not an estimate dressed as a guarantee; still comfortably under the 5-minute
reconciliation threshold PERF-12 treats as the failure line, with the reasoning shown rather than
asserted.

**Scan Lambda timeout: revised to 90s** (one `queryGsi3Page` call + up to 20 `SendMessageBatch`
chunks of â‰¤10 candidates each, each individually retryable per Â§5 â€” 20 chunks Ã— ~100ms typical +
margin for up to 3 chunks needing full 3-attempt backoff in a bad case â‰ˆ 25s realistic worst case,
90s leaves >3x headroom) â†’ scan queue visibility timeout = 540s (module's fixed 6x). **Lease
duration: revised to 200s** (invariant: â‰¥2Ã— scan Lambda timeout = 180s â‰¤ 200s; scan visibility
540s > 200s, preserving the no-redelivery-during-live-lease property with the new numbers). Claim
Lambda/queue unchanged from round 2 (10s timeout / 60s visibility).
**`reserved_concurrent_executions`**: scan queue = **10** (bound from Â§3's â‰¤8 genuinely-concurrent
chains + margin, explicit reasoning replacing round 1/2's "= shard count" oversimplification);
`maximum_concurrency` (event source mapping parameter) = 10, matching. Claim queue:
`reserved_concurrent_executions` = **50**, `maximum_concurrency` = 50 â€” sized against the
single-shard-burst model: 10,000 candidates Ã· 10/batch = 1,000 claim-Lambda batches, at 50
concurrent Ã— ~200ms/batch (this project's existing `reminder-dispatch` claim-shaped Lambda's own
observed latency class, reused as the estimate basis rather than an unmeasured guess) â‰ˆ 4s of
processing time, arriving throughout the ~125s drain window, never backlogged. **`maxReceiveCount
= 5` (module-fixed, unchanged both queues). Batch size: scan = 1 (unchanged reasoning), claim = 10
(matches `reminder-dispatch`'s own existing event-source-mapping batch size,
`infra/main.tf:955-969`'s `reminder_dispatch_from_queue` block â€” to be cited with exact line
numbers against that block in the final artifact). `MaximumBatchingWindowInSeconds`: 0 for scan

## Required change 7: error table â€” corrected reason-specific handling

Codex correctly found today's code treats ANY `TransactionCanceledException` as a lost race
(`producer.ts:309-314`, `document-chasing-producer.ts:112-135`), never inspecting
`getCancellationReasonCodes` (`occ.ts:431-447`) despite that helper existing â€” **this plan
deliberately does NOT preserve that behavior**, it fixes it, since D-299's own text names
"`CancellationReasons`, distinguindo corretamente" as a requirement of the new claim consumer, not
an optional nicety. Revised table:

| Failure | SQS outcome | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| `queryGsi3Page` transient DynamoDB error | `batchItemFailures` (retried) | unchanged from round 2 |
| Malformed scan-continuation payload (schema-invalid) | `batchItemFailures` (retried up to `maxReceiveCount`) + `ScanMessageValidationFailure` metric/alarm at >0 | round 2's "log-only" reversed â€” Codex correctly flagged silent work-unit loss risk; retrying doesn't help a truly malformed message, but it DOES give the alarm time to page before the DLQ absorbs it after 5 tries, and a message that's malformed due to a transient serialization bug (not impossible) gets a chance to succeed on a redeploy before exhausting retries |
| Lease acquire conditional check failed | ack'd, no-op, `LeaseAcquireOutcome{contended}` | unchanged |
| Lease reclaim succeeds | ack'd, `LeaseAcquireOutcome{reclaimed}` | **this IS required change 10's stalled-chain signal â€” see below** |
| Checkpoint conditional check failed (stale/duplicate continuation) | ack'd, no-op | unchanged reasoning, now safe by construction (Â§1-2) |
| `SendMessageBatch` sender-fault entry | invocation throws, `CandidateSenderFault` metric+alarm | reversed per Â§5 |
| Claim consumer `transactWrite` cancelled, occurrence-update entry's reason via `getCancellationReasonCodes` = `ConditionalCheckFailed` | ack'd, no-op (`lost-race`) | the ONLY case that's a true lost race â€” fixed per Codex's finding |
| Claim consumer `transactWrite` cancelled, any OTHER reason (including on the outbox Put entry) | `batchItemFailures` (retried) | genuine transient failure, now correctly distinguished instead of collapsed |
| Unknown GSI3 discriminator | **invocation throws** (restores `shouldAlarm()`'s existing fail-closed behavior, `producer.ts:149-156`) | round 2 wrongly softened this to a no-op; reversed â€” D-039's fail-closed intent is preserved unchanged, not weakened by this redesign |

## Required change 8/10: stalled-chain detection â€” reuses `LeaseAcquireOutcome{reclaimed}`, no new query

No separate periodic reconciliation query is needed: because Â§3's enumeration re-evaluates the
FULL lookback window (15 minutes) on EVERY tick (unchanged from today), any lease that goes stale
is naturally re-encountered and reclaimed within at most one tick interval (60s) of its expiry â€”
the existing `LeaseAcquireOutcome` metric (round 1, dimension `outcome`) already fires
`reclaimed` exactly when this happens. New CloudWatch alarm: `Sum(LeaseAcquireOutcome{outcome=
reclaimed})` `> 0` over any 5-minute period â†’ pages (same alarm topic as the DLQ-age alarms,
`alert_topic_arn`). This is an independent, periodic (piggybacked on the 60s tick, not on a
checkpoint) signal that requires NEITHER an empty-queue-and-no-checkpoint condition (Codex's
critique of round 2's `LeaseAgeAtCheckpoint` approach) NOR a new Lambda/query â€” it reuses work this
design already does every tick. Widget/dashboard JSON: added to
`infra/modules/observability-dashboard/` next to the existing DLQ-age widgets, one new alarm
widget per queue pair â€” exact Terraform resource names left for the implementation session (this
is boilerplate once the metric/alarm exist, not a design decision).

## Required change 13â†’ this round's Â§: deploy/rollback via explicit env-var toggle

Codex's own three suggested options include "a temporary handler-routing/feature switch" â€” this
plan adopts it explicitly, addressing the earlier concern that D-299 "rejected a flag": D-299
rejected PERMANENTLY running old and new claim logic concurrently against the same table (a
correctness/race concern â€” doubling the concurrent-claim surface indefinitely). A **deploy-time-only
env var** (`SCAN_MODE: "LEGACY" | "PAGED"`, read once at cold start, no per-invocation branching
risk) is a materially different, lesser thing: at any given moment exactly ONE mode is live (never
both), and the var is deleted entirely (code for `"LEGACY"` removed) in the third, later change â€”
it is a rollout mechanism with a defined end, not a standing dual-path architecture.
- **Apply 1**: claim queue + consumer (event-source-mapping enabled, inert â€” nothing publishes to
  it), scan queue (event-source-mapping enabled â€” also inert, nothing publishes to it either, since
  `SCAN_MODE=LEGACY` never emits start messages), new port/adapter/handler code deployed but
  `SCAN_MODE=LEGACY` at the environment level keeps `reminder-producer-handler.ts` executing
  exactly today's `runProducerTick` path. This IS enough to make Apply 1 genuinely inert (Codex's
  exact objection to round 2), because the toggle lives in application code reading `process.env`,
  not in Terraform resource wiring whose ordering Terraform doesn't guarantee.
- **Apply 2**: flips `SCAN_MODE=PAGED` via a Lambda environment variable update â€” a single
  Terraform-managed attribute change, applied atomically to the function configuration (no
  cross-resource ordering concern, since it's one resource's one attribute).
- **Lease/queue cleanup on rollback**: revert Apply 2's env var back to `LEGACY`. In-flight scan
  chains stop producing new checkpoints (no consumer reads them meaningfully once `LEGACY` code
  ignores SQS-sourced invocations â€” the SQS-triggered handler branch checks `SCAN_MODE` too and
  no-ops with a log line if rolled back mid-flight, rather than assuming it's never invoked).
  Abandoned lease rows expire via `purgeAfterTtl` (corrected attribute name,
  `infra/modules/dynamo-table/main.tf:206-208` â€” round 2's `ttl` typo fixed) at `leaseUntil + 7d`,
  unchanged from round 1/2's retention choice. Queued-but-unprocessed scan/claim messages age out
  via each queue's normal 4-day retention or get DLQ'd after `maxReceiveCount=5` â€” both bounded,
  self-cleaning, no manual drain step required, though a runbook note (not a blocking step) to
  purge the claim queue manually before an unusually long rollback window is worth adding in the
  final artifact.

## Self-grade (Claude, blind â€” before seeing Codex round 3)

**8.7/10.** The outbox-atomic checkpoint is the real fix this round needed â€” it's not a patch, it
reuses an existing, already-proven mechanism in this exact codebase rather than inventing new
choreography, which is the strongest kind of answer to a Codex correctness objection. Remaining
risk I can see: (a) the "~125s to drain a single-shard 10k burst" bound rests on an unmeasured
2s-per-hop assumption â€” reasonable but still a judgment call, not a citation; (b) I have not
traced `DispatchOutboxRelay`'s actual code to confirm it can be extended to a second destination
routing target as cleanly as described â€” asserted from the `destination`-discriminator doc comment
in `outbox.ts`, not from reading the relay's own implementation file; (c) the env-var toggle's
SQS-triggered-branch no-op-on-rollback behavior is new this round and hasn't been checked against

Lambda concurrency throttling without messages piling up ugly (functionally fine since they'd just

## `reviews/` Ã¢â‚¬â€ convenÃƒÂ§ÃƒÂ£o de nomenclatura e classificaÃƒÂ§ÃƒÂ£o

296:12:## Research declaration (research-protocol.md, E-014)
297:13:
298:14:**SIM PARCIAL.** The macro-pattern (decouple scan from claim via two queues) is already
299:15:externally researched and cited in D-299 (AWS Prescriptive Guidance, Lambda+SQS developer guide,
300:16:SQS API reference). What's new at THIS level is a sub-decision AWS has a well-documented but
301:17:non-obvious answer for: **SQS visibility timeout sizing relative to Lambda timeout, and its
302:18:interaction with `maxReceiveCount`/DLQ redelivery for a handler that holds an idempotency lease**.
303:19:This project's own `sqs-worker-queue` module already encodes one specific answer (6x, fixed,
304:20:`maxReceiveCount=5`) as a blanket rule for the dispatch case ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â applying it unmodified to a
305:21:lease-holding consumer needs to be checked against AWS's own guidance on visibility timeout vs.
306:22:in-flight processing time, because a lease-based state machine changes what "redelivery mid-lease"
307:23:means (D-299's own R3ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Â Ã¢â‚¬â„¢R4 finding). Checklist applied this round, sourced from AWS Lambda Developer
308:24:Guide "Using Lambda with Amazon SQS" (event source mapping / partial batch response) and AWS SQS
309:25:"Amazon SQS visibility timeout" page (both already cited as sources in D-299, re-read here for the
310:26:consumer-timeout-vs-lease-duration angle specifically, no new source needed):
311:27:1. Visibility timeout must exceed **worst-case** processing time, not average ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â for a lease-based
312:28:   consumer, worst case includes lease renewal, not just one page's work.
313:29:2. `maxReceiveCount` ÃƒÆ’Ã¢â‚¬â€ avg processing time bounds how long a poison message cycles before DLQ ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â
314:30:   must be reconciled with lease `leaseUntil` duration so an expired lease and an SQS redelivery
315:31:   don't race in a way that duplicates or drops work (D-299's exact concern, now at the queue-timer
316:32:   level instead of the state-machine level).
317:33:3. Batch size for the scan-continuation queue must stay effectively 1 (see Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â§3 below) ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â AWS's own
318:34:   guidance warns partial-batch-failure handling gets materially harder above batch size 1 when
319:35:   messages are causally chained (continuation N+1 must not be visible before N's page commits).
320:36:
321:37:## 1. Names
322:38:
323:39:Following `infra/main.tf`'s existing convention (`module "reminder_producer"` /
324:40:`function_name = "${local.name_prefix}-reminder-producer"`, and `reminder-dispatch`'s two-worker
325:41:pattern: `module.dispatch_queue` + `module.reminder_dispatch`):
326:42:
327:43:- **Scan queue** (continuation messages only): Terraform module `module.reminder_scan_queue`,
328:44:  queue name `${local.name_prefix}-reminder-scan`, DLQ `${local.name_prefix}-reminder-scan-dlq`
329:45:  (module's own fixed `-dlq` suffix).
330:46:- **Claim queue** (per-occurrence candidates): `module.reminder_claim_queue`, queue name
331:47:  `${local.name_prefix}-reminder-claim`, DLQ `${local.name_prefix}-reminder-claim-dlq`.
332:48:- **Scan handler**: existing `reminder-producer-handler.ts` is repurposed (not replaced) ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â same
333:49:  Lambda (`module.reminder_producer`, `reminder-producer-handler`), same sole holder of
334:50:  `gsi3_read`. Its trigger becomes dual: EventBridge Scheduler (tick start, one message per
335:51:  eligible shard/minute ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â unchanged entry point) **and** `module.reminder_scan_queue` (continuation
336:52:  messages, same handler, discriminated by event shape: `ReminderProducerEvent` vs. new
337:53:  `ReminderScanContinuationEvent`).
338:54:- **Claim handler**: new Lambda, following the `reminder-dispatch` naming pattern exactly ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â
339:55:  `module.reminder_claim_consumer`, `function_name = "${local.name_prefix}-reminder-claim-consumer"`,
340:56:  `handler_name = "reminder-claim-consumer-handler"`, source file
341:57:  `src/runtime/aws/handlers/reminder-claim-consumer-handler.ts`.
342:58:- **Page-lease table**: reuses the **main table** (no new table ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â D-299 says "mesma tabela
343:59:  principal"), item shape below.
344:60:- **Outbox destinations** (new `OutboxDestination` union members in `src/shared/outbox/outbox.ts`,
345:61:  same file/pattern as `SQS_REMINDER_DISPATCH_V1` etc.): `SQS_REMINDER_SCAN_CONTINUATION_V1` and
346:62:  `SQS_REMINDER_CLAIM_CANDIDATE_V1`. **Correction from architecture round**: the scan step's own
347:63:  candidate-publish + continuation-publish + lease-write are NOT all in one DynamoDB transaction
348:64:  (SQS `SendMessageBatch` cannot participate in `TransactWriteItems`) ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â see Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â§4 for how outbox is
349:65:  actually used here vs. the direct-relay pattern.
350:66:- **Worker module** (pure logic, clock-injected, observability-agnostic per AGENTS.md Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â§7):
351:67:  `src/workers/reminder-scan/scan-page.ts` (one page of `queryGsi3` ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Â Ã¢â‚¬â„¢ candidates + next lease
352:68:  state) and `src/workers/reminder-claim/claim-occurrence.ts` (the existing claim logic extracted
353:69:  from today's `runProducerTick`, now callable per-candidate instead of per-shard-loop).
354:70:
355:71:## 2. Page-lease state machine
356:72:
357:73:**Item** (main table, single-table design ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â PK/SK pattern matches existing shard-scan items in
358:74:`dynamodb-reminder-producer-store.ts`, confirmed against that file):
359:75:
360:76:```
361:77:PK: SCAN#<shardId>#<tickMinuteISO>     e.g. SCAN#3#2026-09-14T22:31:00Z
362:78:SK: LEASE
363:79:entityType: "ReminderScanLease"
364:80:status: "IN_PROGRESS" | "COMPLETED"
365:81:ownerToken: string (randomUUID, one per Lambda invocation attempt ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â NOT per SQS messageId,
366:82:            so a redelivered SQS message that re-enters the same invocation semantics gets a
367:83:            fresh token and must re-win the conditional acquire, closing the exact silent-drop
368:84:            hole D-299 R3 found in the stateless-fence design)
369:85:leaseUntil: number (epoch ms)
370:86:lastEvaluatedKey: string | undefined (JSON-serialized DynamoDB ExclusiveStartKey for queryGsi3,
371:87:            undefined on the first page, present on every continuation)
372:88:pagesProcessed: number
373:89:candidatesPublished: number
374:90:version: number (occ.ts optimistic concurrency, same convention as every other mutable item)
375:91:ttl: epoch seconds, 7 days after leaseUntil ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â cheap cleanup, matches this project's existing TTL
376:92:     convention on other transient coordination items (checked against `defaultShardConfig()`'s
377:93:     neighbors in dynamodb-reminder-producer-store.ts)
378:94:```
379:95:
380:96:**Acquire** (first page of a shard/minute, or reclaim after expiry) ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â `occ.ts`'s
381:97:`buildConditionalPut` with:
382:98:`ConditionExpression: "attribute_not_exists(PK) OR (status = :inProgress AND leaseUntil < :now) OR status = :completedNoop"`
383:99:ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â the third arm exists only to make a duplicate "start" message (a Scheduler retry firing the same
384:100:shard/minute twice) a safe no-op rather than an error; it still writes nothing new when already
385:101:`COMPLETED` (checked in application code before the Put, not relied on as a silent race ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â same
386:102:"belt AND suspenders" pattern `runProducerTick` already uses for claim races today).
387:103:
388:104:**Renew** (before publishing each continuation) ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â `occ.ts`'s `buildVersionedUpdate` with
389:105:`ConditionExpression: "ownerToken = :myToken AND version = :expectedVersion"`: sets new
390:106:`leaseUntil`, `lastEvaluatedKey`, increments `pagesProcessed`/`candidatesPublished`, bumps
391:107:`version`. **This update happens AFTER the claim-queue `SendMessageBatch` succeeds and BEFORE the
392:108:continuation message is sent** ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â ordering matters: if the process dies between the batch send and
393:109:the lease renew, the next attempt (a fresh SQS redelivery of the SAME scan message, since it never
394:110:completed) re-reads `lastEvaluatedKey` from the STALE lease state (pre-this-page), re-queries the
395:111:same page from `queryGsi3` (deterministic per `lastEvaluatedKey`), and re-publishes the same
396:112:candidates. This is why **claim-queue candidates must be idempotent to redelivery independent of
397:113:this lease** ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â already true by construction, because the claim consumer's own conditional
398:114:`transactWrite` (Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â§ below) is the actual idempotency boundary for claiming, not the scan side. The
399:115:lease's job is only to make forward SCAN progress resumable exactly-once-effectively, not to
400:116:dedupe claims (that guarantee already exists one layer down).
401:117:
402:118:**Release** (last page, `queryGsi3` returns no `LastEvaluatedKey`) ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â `buildVersionedUpdate` sets
403:119:`status = "COMPLETED"`, same ownerToken/version condition.
404:120:
405:121:**Expire**: no active "expire" write ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â a lease simply becomes reclaimable once `leaseUntil < now`,
406:122:matched by the Acquire condition above. No separate reconciliation pass is added for this (see Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â§6
407:123:ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â `reminder-reconciliation.ts` is untouched; lease reclaim is self-contained inside the scan path,
408:124:triggered by the SAME continuation message that would have fired next, since EventBridge Scheduler
409:125:fires a new tick every minute and a new tick for an ALREADY in-progress shard is the natural
410:126:reclaim trigger ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â see Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â§7 for why this is safe rather than racy).
411:127:
412:128:## 3. Timeout/visibility sizing
413:129:
414:130:Fixed module facts (not renegotiable without a `sqs-worker-queue` module change, out of scope
415:131:here): `visibility_timeout_seconds = consumer_timeout_seconds * 6`, `maxReceiveCount = 5` fixed.
416:132:
417:133:- **Scan Lambda timeout**: 30s (one `queryGsi3` page + one `SendMessageBatch` + one lease
418:134:  renew/acquire ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â bounded work, generous margin over p99). ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Â Ã¢â‚¬â„¢ scan queue visibility timeout = 180s
419:135:  (module-derived, 6x).
420:136:- **Claim Lambda timeout**: 10s (unchanged from today's per-occurrence claim ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â a single `get` +
421:137:  `transactWrite`, same cost as today's inner loop iteration). ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Â Ã¢â‚¬â„¢ claim queue visibility timeout =
422:138:  60s (module-derived, 6x).
423:139:- **Lease duration** (`leaseUntil - leaseAcquiredAt`): **90s** ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â set independently of the Lambda
424:140:  timeout (it is a business-level mutual-exclusion window, not a retry mechanism) but sized against
425:141:  it with an explicit invariant: **lease duration ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Â°Ã‚Â¥ 2x scan Lambda timeout** (30sÃƒÆ’Ã¢â‚¬â€2=60s ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Â°Ã‚Â¤ 90s),
426:142:  giving one full retry's worth of headroom before a DIFFERENT invocation is allowed to steal the
427:143:  lease, so a slow-but-alive attempt is never pre-empted by its own SQS-triggered retry racing in.
428:144:  Combined with **scan visibility timeout (180s) > lease duration (90s)**, an SQS redelivery of the
429:145:  SAME message can never arrive before the lease it would contend with has already legitimately
430:146:  expired ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â removing the specific race D-299 R3 found (two live workers believing they both hold
431:147:  the lease) by construction, not by luck.
432:148:- **`maxReceiveCount=5` (fixed)** on the scan queue means a poison continuation message cycles for
433:149:  up to 5ÃƒÆ’Ã¢â‚¬â€180s = 900s (15 min) before DLQ ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â acceptable, since EventBridge Scheduler fires a new
434:150:  tick every 60s regardless, so a stuck shard's lease will be reclaimed by a FRESH tick's message
435:151:  well before the poison copy DLQs; the DLQ path exists for the case where `queryGsi3` itself is
436:152:  erroring (data/query bug), not for ordinary transient contention.
437:153:- **Batch size**: scan queue consumer batch size = **1** (continuation messages are causally
438:154:  chained per shard ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â processing two "next page" messages for the same shard concurrently is
439:155:  exactly the race this design eliminates via the lease, so the event-source-mapping must not
440:156:  create that race by delivering >1 at once). Claim queue consumer batch size = **10** (candidates
441:157:  are independent per occurrence, matches `reminder-dispatch`'s existing batch size ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â confirmed
442:158:  against `infra/main.tf`'s `reminder_dispatch_from_queue` event source mapping).
443:159:- **Concurrency invariant** (D-299, now with numbers): scan queue
444:160:  `reserved_concurrent_executions` = number of shards (`defaultShardConfig()`'s shard count,
445:161:  confirmed = `DEFAULT_SHARD_COUNT = 4` in `src/modules/reminder/domain/shard-config.ts`) ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â one in-flight scan per shard by
446:162:  construction (the lease already enforces this logically; the Lambda concurrency cap is defense in
447:163:  depth, cheap to set). Claim queue `reserved_concurrent_executions` = **16** (ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Â°Ã‚Â¥ sum of scan's
448:164:  per-page candidate fan-out ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â a page of `queryGsi3` batches up to 25 candidates per
449:165:  `SendMessageBatch` call, ÃƒÆ’Ã¢â‚¬â€4 shards worst-case-concurrent = 100 theoretical peak sends, but claim
450:166:  Lambda p50 is <200ms so 16 concurrent claim workers clears a 100-item burst in ~1.3s ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â matches
451:167:  PERF-12's own 10k-in-a-minute volume target with margin, verified against PERF-12's report
452:168:  numbers in `docs/architecture/reviews/reminder-producer-structural-fix-scoping/` round artifacts).
453:169:
454:170:## 4. Tracing/logging/metrics/errors/outbox/writes ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â concrete
455:171:
456:172:- **Correlation ID propagation**: the ORIGINAL scan tick's `randomUUID()` (today's
457:173:  `reminder-producer-handler.ts` behavior, unchanged) is carried as an SQS `MessageAttribute`
458:174:  named `correlationId` on EVERY message this mechanism sends ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â both the scan-continuation message
459:175:  and every claim-candidate message in a page's `SendMessageBatch` ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â using the EXACT mechanism
460:176:  `correlationIdFromSqsRecord()`/`outboxRecordCorrelationId` already establishes for
461:177:  `reminder-dispatch` (same attribute name, same sender-side convention in
462:178:  `src/runtime/aws/composition/*.ts`). The scan handler wraps ALL of its work (including
463:179:  continuation re-entry) in `runWithContext({ correlationId }, ...)`, reading the attribute via
464:180:  `correlationIdFromSqsRecord()` when triggered by SQS and using `randomUUID()` only on the
465:181:  EventBridge Scheduler entry point (page 1 of a fresh tick) ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â same branch shape as today's
466:182:  handler. The claim consumer does the same on its inbound message. Net effect: one
467:183:  `correlationId` traces a shard/minute's entire page-by-page scan AND every claim it produced,
468:184:  queryable end-to-end via CloudWatch Logs Insights.
469:185:- **Logging** (`SecureLogger`, no raw `console.*`): new event names ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â
470:186:  `"reminder-scan page complete"` (fields: `shardId`, `tickMinute`, `pageNumber`,
471:187:  `candidatesPublished`, `hasMore`), `"reminder-scan lease acquire failed"` (fields: `shardId`,
472:188:  `tickMinute`, `reason: "already-in-progress" | "conditional-check-failed"`),
473:189:  `"reminder-claim occurrence claimed"` / `"reminder-claim occurrence lost race"` (fields:
474:190:  `occurrenceId` type-discriminated per D-299's `GSI3SK` distinction, `outcome`).
475:191:- **Metrics** (`emitMetric`, EMF, namespace `ExpirationTracker/ReminderProducer` for the scan side
476:192:  reusing the existing namespace since it's the same Lambda, and a NEW namespace
477:193:  `ExpirationTracker/ReminderClaimConsumer` for the new Lambda, matching the
478:194:  per-service-namespace convention `metrics.ts` documents):
479:195:  - `ReminderProducer`: `PagesScanned` (Count, no dimensions), `CandidatesPublishedPerPage` (Count,
480:196:    dimension `entityType` ÃƒÂ¢Ã‹â€ Ã‹â€  {`ReminderOccurrence`,`DocumentChasingOccurrence`} ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â closed 2-value
481:197:    union, safe per dimension-cardinality rule), `LeaseAcquireOutcome` (Count, dimension `outcome`
482:198:    ÃƒÂ¢Ã‹â€ Ã‹â€  {`acquired`,`reclaimed`,`contended`} ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â closed 3-value union).
483:199:  - `ReminderClaimConsumer`: `ClaimOutcome` (Count, dimension `outcome` ÃƒÂ¢Ã‹â€ Ã‹â€ 
484:200:    {`claimed`,`lost-race`,`unknown-entity-type`} ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â closed union, same shape as today's
485:201:    `runProducerTick` result fields), `ClaimQueueBacklogAge` ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â **not emitted by the handler**;
486:202:    already covered natively by the module's `ApproximateAgeOfOldestMessage` CloudWatch alarm
487:203:    (D-299 explicitly names this as native, not a custom metric ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â kept consistent here rather than
488:204:    duplicating).
489:205:- **Error taxonomy** (`app-error.ts`): a lease acquire race that loses is NOT an error (expected
490:206:  contention, logged/metric'd only). A `queryGsi3` failure inside the scan page throws the SAME
491:207:  taxonomy the current handler already uses (`ValidationError` for bad continuation payload shape,
492:208:  unchanged AppError subclasses for downstream failures ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â no new subclass needed, confirmed by
493:209:  reading the union in `app-error.ts`; if a future round finds a gap, add
494:210:  `ReminderLeaseConflictError extends AppError` only if contention needs to surface as a retryable
495:211:  error rather than a logged no-op ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â deferred as a round-2 open question, not assumed here).
496:212:- **Outbox**: candidates and the continuation message are **NOT** written via the transactional
497:213:  outbox pattern, and this is a deliberate deviation from AGENTS.md's "critical side-effect in the
498:214:  same transaction as the aggregate write" rule ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â because there IS no aggregate write at scan time
499:215:  (the scan step only reads GSI3 and writes its OWN lease item; the occurrence aggregate write only
500:216:  happens later, in the claim consumer). The outbox pattern's applicability is at the CLAIM step:
501:217:  the claim consumer's existing `get`+`transactWrite` (unchanged from today) is the aggregate
502:218:  write, and it already should (today's code should be checked, not assumed ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â round 2 action item)
503:219:  carry its resulting event via the SAME `TransactWriteItems`, exactly like `SQS_REMINDER_DISPATCH_V1`
504:220:  today. Round 1 conclusion: **outbox governs the claimÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Â Ã¢â‚¬â„¢dispatch boundary (unchanged from today),
505:221:  not the scanÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Â Ã¢â‚¬â„¢claim boundary (new, and necessarily a direct `SendMessageBatch`, not outbox-mediated,
506:222:  because outbox requires a DynamoDB transaction and the scan step's transaction is the lease
507:223:  write, which is unrelated to the individual candidates being published)**.
508:224:- **DynamoDB writes**: lease acquire/renew/release exclusively via `occ.ts`'s
509:225:  `buildConditionalPut`/`buildVersionedUpdate` (no raw `PutItem`/`UpdateItem`), confirmed pattern
510:226:  match against existing shard-scan-state usage in `dynamodb-reminder-producer-store.ts`.

512:228:## 5. Test plan
513:229:
514:230:- **Unit** (`test/unit/reminder/`, following existing `in-memory-store.ts` fixture pattern):
515:231:  page-lease acquire/renew/release pure logic ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â concurrent acquire attempts (both should not
516:232:  succeed), renew with stale `ownerToken` (must fail), renew with correct token but expired
517:233:  `leaseUntil` (must fail ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â a zombie holder cannot renew past its own expiry), release from wrong
518:234:  owner (must fail), reclaim after expiry (must succeed for a NEW ownerToken), redelivery-of-same-
519:235:  message-mid-lease (must be a safe no-op re-publish, not a double-claim ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â this is the exact D-299
520:236:  R3 finding, gets its own dedicated test).
521:237:- **Integration**: extend the EXISTING GSI3-isolation coverage ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â this codebase's actual mechanism
522:238:  is `infra/tests/stack.tftest.hcl` (Terraform test asserting IAM policy scoping to GSI3, not a
523:239:  `.test.ts` file of that exact name ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â corrected from the task prompt's assumption after checking;
524:240:  no `test/integration/gsi3-isolation.test.ts` exists in this repo today). Add a new
525:241:  `terraform test` assertion (same file, new `run` block) that the NEW `reminder_claim_consumer`
526:242:  Lambda's IAM role has NO `gsi3_read` statement, mirroring the existing assertion pattern for
527:243:  `reminder_dispatch`.
528:244:- **Integration** (application-level, Vitest): a scanÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Â Ã¢â‚¬â„¢claim round trip using the in-memory SQS +
529:245:  DynamoDB test doubles this codebase already has for `reminder-dispatch` (composition root
530:246:  fixtures) ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â burst volume at PERF-12's 10k scale, asserting ZERO loss (the actual regression this
531:247:  whole design fixes) and that pausing/resuming a shard mid-scan (simulated Lambda death) via a
532:248:  fresh invocation with the same continuation message reaches `COMPLETED` with all candidates
533:249:  published exactly once each.

535:251:## 6. `reminder-reconciliation.ts` impact
536:252:
537:253:**Confirmed: no change needed**, with actual reasoning (not just repeating D-299's stated
538:254:expectation): `reminder-reconciliation.ts`'s job (per its own file, to be re-read in round 2 for a
539:255:citation-level confirmation) is to catch occurrences stuck in `CLAIMED` past `claimExpiresAt` ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â
540:256:that contract is entirely downstream of the claim consumer's `transactWrite`, which writes
541:257:`claimExpiresAt` identically to today's code (D-299's own premise, unchanged by this plan since the
542:258:claim logic itself is only relocated, not rewritten). The scan-side lease this plan adds is a
543:259:DIFFERENT state machine on a DIFFERENT item (`SCAN#...#LEASE`, never `CLAIMED` occurrence rows) that
544:260:reconciliation never reads today and has no reason to start reading ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â a stuck scan lease
545:261:self-heals via the next EventBridge tick's reclaim path (Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â§2), not via reconciliation. One residual
546:262:open question for round 2: does reconciliation's own scan of `CLAIMED` rows need its OWN
547:263:correlation ID propagation update for consistency, even though its logic doesn't change? (Leaning
548:264:no ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â it's not part of this mechanism's message chain ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â but flagging rather than asserting.)
549:265:
550:266:## 7. Migration/rollout
551:267:
552:268:Big-bang cutover, not staged, for a concrete reason: the scan and claim halves are not
553:269:independently useful (a scan queue with no claim consumer just accumulates candidates; a claim
554:270:consumer with no new-shape scan producer never receives anything) ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â there's no safe intermediate
555:271:state to stage through, unlike, say, a dual-write migration. Sequencing:
556:272:1. Deploy claim consumer Lambda + claim queue (inert ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â nothing publishes to it yet).
557:273:2. Deploy scan queue (inert ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â nothing subscribes to the OLD producer's shard-loop yet, since it
558:274:   doesn't publish to it).
559:275:3. Deploy the MODIFIED `reminder-producer-handler.ts` (now page-based) in the SAME release as step
560:276:   1/2's infra ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â this is the actual cutover moment; the old monolithic-per-shard loop code path is
561:277:   deleted in this same change, not kept behind a flag (D-299 didn't ask for a flag, and a flag
562:278:   here would mean maintaining two claim code paths against the same table, doubling the
563:279:   concurrent-claim race surface this whole fix targets).
564:280:4. **Occurrences already `SCHEDULED` at cutover**: confirmed safe, with reasoning ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â `SCHEDULED`
565:281:   occurrences are discovered by `queryGsi3`, not by any in-flight queue state; the OLD mechanism's
566:282:   only in-flight artifact at cutover is whatever's already sitting in the OLD single-invocation
567:283:   claim loop of a tick that started before deploy (which either finishes normally before the
568:284:   deploy completes, since Lambda in-flight invocations aren't killed by a code update, or times
569:285:   out and is picked up fresh by the NEW scan mechanism's next tick ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â no occurrence-level state is
570:286:   lost either way, since `SCHEDULED` occurrences are read fresh from GSI3 every tick regardless of
571:287:   which mechanism is running).
572:288:5. Rollback path: revert step 3's Lambda code only (keep the new queues/consumer deployed but
573:289:   inert) ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â since GSI3 access never moved, a revert to the old handler code resumes the old
574:290:   monolithic scan immediately with no data migration needed in either direction.

844:255:module "reminder_producer" {
845:256:  source = "./modules/lambda-function"
846:257:
847:258:  function_name = "${local.name_prefix}-reminder-producer"
848:259:  handler_name  = "reminder-producer-handler"
849:260:  source_dir    = "${local.dist_dir}/reminder-producer-handler"
850:261:  # PERF-12 1k load test (docs/engineering/performance/results/PERF-12-async-pipeline-1k.md):
851:262:  # the CDK-inherited 10s default was exceeded for 7 straight minutes under a realistic burst
852:263:  # (many occurrences due the same minute), fully sequential per-occurrence processing, no
853:264:  # parallelism at the time. Raised to 60s: producer.ts now processes occurrences with bounded
854:265:  # concurrency (PRODUCER_CLAIM_CONCURRENCY=8), so a get+transactWrite pair costing tens of ms
855:266:  # (PERF-12's own measurement) puts a burst of ~1,000 occurrences well under this budget even
856:267:  # with generous headroom for DynamoDB latency variance - not raised to Lambda's 900s max,
857:268:  # which would let a genuinely pathological tick run for 15 minutes before EventBridge's next
858:269:  # 1-minute-later invocation piles another one on top of it.
859:270:  timeout_seconds                = 60
860:271:  adot_layer_arn                 = var.adot_layer_arn
861:272:  environment_variables          = local.common_env
862:273:  reserved_concurrent_executions = var.enable_reserved_concurrency ? 2 : null

1299:710:# D-233: SEC-R2-02 fix. Two changes from the original mapping:
1300:711:#  - filter_criteria now also matches on entityType - the marker's OWN Put/Update/Delete writes
1301:712:#    (D-233's new claim/lease mechanism) already generate stream INSERT/MODIFY events on this
1302:713:#    same table; without this filter they'd reach the handler, get classified "malformed" by
1303:714:#    isDeliveryRecord(), and inflate batchItemFailures/the failure queue with pure noise (a latent
1304:715:#    bug that predates D-233 too, since claim()'s original PutItem already wrote a marker row).
1305:716:#  - maximum_retry_attempts/maximum_record_age_in_seconds set to -1 (unlimited, bounded only by
1306:717:#    DynamoDB Streams' own native 24h retention) - a bounded retry count/age (the previous
1307:718:#    3/3600) could exhaust BEFORE the marker's 30s claim lease ever expires, leaving
1308:719:#    SKIPPED_LEASE_ACTIVE retries stuck with no path to the SEND_UNCERTAIN reconciliation
1309:720:#    deliver.ts relies on. The IteratorAge alarm below is the real backstop for a genuinely
1310:721:#    stuck/poison record - it fires in minutes, not after the 24h native retention discards it.

5401:FILE src/shared/observability/context.ts
5402:1:/**
5403:2: * Request-scoped correlation context via AsyncLocalStorage (m5-observability-design.md #2).
5404:3: * runWithContext is called once per record for batch handlers (SQS, DynamoDB Streams, sweeper) -
5405:4: * never once per invocation for those - so context never leaks across records in the same batch.
5406:5: */
5407:6:import { AsyncLocalStorage } from "node:async_hooks";
5408:7:
5409:8:export interface RequestContext {
5410:9:  correlationId: string;
5411:10:  tenantId?: string;
5412:11:  requestId?: string;
5413:12:}
5414:13:
5415:14:const storage = new AsyncLocalStorage<RequestContext>();
5416:15:
5417:16:export function runWithContext<T>(context: RequestContext, fn: () => T): T {
5418:17:  return storage.run(context, fn);
5419:18:}
5420:19:
5421:20:export function getContext(): RequestContext | undefined {
5422:21:  return storage.getStore();
5423:22:}
5424:23:
5425:24:/**
5426:25: * m5-observability-design.md #2: correlationId for an SQS record whose sender (relay/
5427:26: * sweeper's composition-root senders, src/runtime/aws/composition/*.ts) propagates the
5428:27: * original business correlationId via this exact MessageAttribute name - see
5429:28: * outboxRecordCorrelationId (src/shared/outbox/outbox.ts) for the sender side of this same
5430:29: * contract. Falls back to the SQS messageId only for a message that never got the
5431:30: * attribute (pre-M5 in-flight, or a queue whose producer has no upstream correlationId to
5432:31: * propagate, e.g. SES/SNS-sourced messages) - pulled out as its own pure function so the
5433:32: * extraction itself is unit-testable without a handler module's side-effecting top-level
5434:33: * AWS client construction.
5435:34: */
5436:35:export function correlationIdFromSqsRecord(record: { messageAttributes?: Record<string, { stringValue?: string }>; messageId: string }): string {
5437:36:  return record.messageAttributes?.["correlationId"]?.stringValue ?? record.messageId;
5438:37:}

5449:10: * (`AGENTS.md` Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â§7/E-007). Only the real Lambda handlers in `src/runtime/aws/handlers/` call
5450:11: * this, right next to the `logger.info(..., { outcome: ... })` call that already exists there.
5451:12: *

5453:14: * `logger.ts` precedent)**: `tenantId` (or any other high-cardinality value ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â a user id, a
5454:15: * request id) must NEVER be a metric dimension ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â each unique dimension combination is a
5455:16: * separately-billed custom metric, and tenant count grows without bound. `Outcome` values used
5456:17: * as dimensions here are closed, low-cardinality unions (5-9 members, enumerated at each real
5457:18: * call site) ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â safe. Per-tenant investigation is a CloudWatch Logs Insights query against the
5458:19: * structured logs (which already carry `tenantId` via `runWithContext`), never a metric
5459:20: * dimension ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â see `infra/modules/observability-dashboard/`'s log widgets.
5460:21: */

5467:28:   * destination name) ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â never a tenantId/userId/requestId. See the module doc comment above. */

5494:55:

5499:60: */

5503:64:  } catch {

5505:66:    // logger itself could be the thing failing in a truly pathological case); this is the one
5506:67:    // place in the codebase allowed to fail completely silently, by design.
5507:68:  }

5565:56:interface ScopeCondition {
5566:57:  namePlaceholder: string;
5567:58:  attributeName: string;
5568:59:  valuePlaceholder: string;
5569:60:  value: string;

5571:62:
5572:63:interface ScopedVersionedUpdateInput {
5573:64:  tableName: string;
5574:65:  key: EntityKey;
5575:66:  expectedVersion: number;
5576:67:  set: Record<string, unknown>;
5577:68:  remove?: string[];
5578:69:  now?: string;
5579:70:  extraConditions?: Array<{ expression: string; names?: Record<string, string>; values?: Record<string, unknown> }>;
5580:71:}
5581:72:
5582:73:/**
5583:74: * Private core shared by `buildVersionedUpdate()` (tenant-fenced, every ordinary business
5584:75: * entity) and `buildAccountScopedVersionedUpdate()` (D-197 fatia 3/5: WhatsApp `WebhookInbox`,
5585:76: * the first entity in this repo with no tenant at all - see
5586:77: * `docs/architecture/reviews/whatsapp-channel-scoping/webhook-inbox-purge-scoping/` for the
5587:78: * 3-round Claude<->Codex protocol, both final notes >=9.0, that decided this shape). The ONLY
5588:79: * difference between the two public builders is which attribute anchors the scope fence
5589:80: * (`tenantId` vs `accountId`) - version increment, `updatedAt`, SET/REMOVE generation,
5590:81: * `extraConditions` composition and placeholder-collision detection are a single implementation,
5591:82: * never duplicated, so the two builders can never drift apart on anything but their fence.
5592:83: */
5593:84:function buildScopedVersionedUpdate(input: ScopedVersionedUpdateInput, scope: ScopeCondition): DynamoUpdateCommandInput {
5594:85:  const now = input.now ?? new Date().toISOString();
5595:86:
5596:87:  const names: Record<string, string> = {
5597:88:    "#version": "version",
5598:89:    [scope.namePlaceholder]: scope.attributeName,
5599:90:    "#updatedAt": "updatedAt",
5600:91:  };
5601:92:  const values: Record<string, unknown> = {
5602:93:    ":expectedVersion": input.expectedVersion,
5603:94:    [scope.valuePlaceholder]: scope.value,
5604:95:    ":one": 1,
5605:96:    ":now": now,
5606:97:  };
5607:98:
5608:99:  const setClauses = ["#version = #version + :one", "#updatedAt = :now"];
5609:100:  let i = 0;
5610:101:  for (const [field, value] of Object.entries(input.set)) {
5611:102:    const nameKey = `#set${i}`;
5612:103:    const valueKey = `:set${i}`;
5613:104:    names[nameKey] = field;
5614:105:    values[valueKey] = value;
5615:106:    setClauses.push(`${nameKey} = ${valueKey}`);
5616:107:    i += 1;
5617:108:  }
5618:109:
5619:110:  const removeClauses: string[] = [];
5620:111:  let j = 0;
5621:112:  for (const field of input.remove ?? []) {
5622:113:    const nameKey = `#rem${j}`;
5623:114:    names[nameKey] = field;
5624:115:    removeClauses.push(nameKey);
5625:116:    j += 1;
5626:117:  }
5627:118:
5628:119:  const expression =
5629:120:    removeClauses.length > 0
5630:121:      ? `SET ${setClauses.join(", ")} REMOVE ${removeClauses.join(", ")}`
5631:122:      : `SET ${setClauses.join(", ")}`;
5632:123:
5633:124:  const baseConditionParts = ["attribute_exists(PK)", "attribute_exists(SK)", "#version = :expectedVersion", `${scope.namePlaceholder} = ${scope.valuePlaceholder}`];
5634:125:  for (const extra of input.extraConditions ?? []) {
5635:126:    for (const [nameKey, name] of Object.entries(extra.names ?? {})) {
5636:127:      if (nameKey in names) throw new Error(`extraConditions name placeholder collides with a reserved/generated key: ${nameKey}`);
5637:128:      names[nameKey] = name;
5638:129:    }
5639:130:    for (const [valueKey, value] of Object.entries(extra.values ?? {})) {
5640:131:      if (valueKey in values) throw new Error(`extraConditions value placeholder collides with a reserved/generated key: ${valueKey}`);
5641:132:      values[valueKey] = value;
5642:133:    }
5643:134:    baseConditionParts.push(`(${extra.expression})`);
5644:135:  }
5645:136:
5646:137:  return {
5647:138:    TableName: input.tableName,
5648:139:    Key: input.key,
5649:140:    UpdateExpression: expression,
5650:141:    ConditionExpression: baseConditionParts.join(" AND "),
5651:142:    ExpressionAttributeNames: names,
5652:143:    ExpressionAttributeValues: values,
5653:144:  };
5654:145:}
5655:146:
5656:147:/**
5657:148: * Builds an UpdateItem input enforcing implementation-blueprint.md #5.2's exact
5658:149: * ConditionExpression: attribute_exists(PK) AND attribute_exists(SK) AND
5659:150: * #version = :expectedVersion AND #tenantId = :tenantId, and increments version atomically.
5660:151: * Contractually unchanged by the account-scoped sibling below - same signature, same generated
5661:152: * expression, byte-for-byte, for every one of this repo's ~40 existing call sites.
5662:153: */
5663:154:export function buildVersionedUpdate(input: VersionedUpdateInput): DynamoUpdateCommandInput {
5664:155:  return buildScopedVersionedUpdate(input, { namePlaceholder: "#tenantId", attributeName: "tenantId", valuePlaceholder: ":tenantId", value: input.tenantId });
5665:156:}

5847:338:/**
5848:339: * Builds a TransactWriteItems `ConditionCheck` entry asserting a row is still at an
5849:340: * expected version (and, optionally, still holds a given attribute value) - used to fence
5850:341: * a commit against a fact read earlier in the same operation but not itself written by
5851:342: * this transaction (e.g. reminder dispatch asserting the ReminderPolicy it read is still
5852:343: * enabled at the version it read, per the BLOCKER-B freshness-fencing fix: reading a row
5853:344: * and later writing elsewhere based on that read is a TOCTOU gap unless the read fact is
5854:345: * re-asserted atomically inside the same TransactWriteItems as the write it gates).
5855:346: */
5856:347:export function buildVersionConditionCheck(input: {
5857:348:  tableName: string;
5858:349:  key: EntityKey;
5859:350:  expectedVersion: number;
5860:351:  /** Extra attribute=value equality conditions beyond version, e.g. { enabled: true, status: "ACTIVE" }. */
5861:352:  extra?: Record<string, unknown>;

6296:105:export interface ProducerTickResult {

6310:119:function minuteFloor(d: Date): Date {
6311:120:  return new Date(Math.floor(d.getTime() / 60_000) * 60_000);
6312:121:}
6313:122:
6314:123:/**
6315:124: * PERF-12 1k load test finding (docs/engineering/performance/results/PERF-12-async-pipeline-1k.md):
6316:125: * this loop used to process one occurrence at a time - one `store.get` + one
6317:126: * `store.transactWrite` per occurrence, fully sequential - inside a Lambda with (at the time)
6318:127: * a 10s timeout. With ~250 occurrences concentrated in one shard/minute under a realistic
6319:128: * burst, that budget was nowhere near enough, the function was killed mid-loop repeatedly, and
6320:129: * occurrences that hadn't been claimed yet eventually aged out of the lookback window,
6321:130: * permanently stuck in SCHEDULED. Bounded concurrency here mirrors the exact pattern already
6322:131: * used for the same reason in reminder-dispatch-handler.ts (D-170) - each occurrence's own
6323:132: * `transactWrite` stays a single, independent atomic conditional claim (never merged across
6324:133: * occurrences), so parallelizing here does not touch the transactional or idempotency
6325:134: * guarantees of any individual claim, only how many claims run concurrently. A plain numeric
6326:135: * constant, not unbounded `Promise.all`, to keep the burst of concurrent DynamoDB round trips
6327:136: * per invocation predictable.
6328:137: */
6329:138:const PRODUCER_CLAIM_CONCURRENCY = 8;
6330:139:
6331:140:/**
6332:141: * Pure alarm decision, extracted so the Lambda handler's "when should this tick throw" logic
6333:142: * is unit-testable without mocking the whole handler/composition root (achado real de revisÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â£o
6334:143: * adversarial, D-039/D-046/D-048: an earlier version of this fail-closed path was silently
6335:144: * absorbed by the handler - `unknownEntityType` was counted but nothing ever read it). Two
6336:145: * independent reasons, checked in this order for a stable, deterministic message:
6337:146: * unrecognized GSI3SK shape (fail-closed, never a retry-race) first, then genuine per-occurrence
6338:147: * claim failures.
6339:148: */
6340:149:export function shouldAlarm(result: ProducerTickResult): { alarm: boolean; reason?: string } {
6341:150:  if (result.unknownEntityType > 0) {
6342:151:    return { alarm: true, reason: `reminder-producer: ${result.unknownEntityType} GSI3 row(s) matched neither the reminder nor the chasing entityType - fail-closed` };
6343:152:  }
6344:153:  if (result.failed.length > 0) {
6345:154:    return { alarm: true, reason: `reminder-producer: ${result.failed.length} occurrence(s) failed to claim` };
6346:155:  }
6347:156:  return { alarm: false };
6348:157:}

6350:159:/** Runs one producer tick for wall-clock minute `tickMinute` (already floored to the minute by the caller/Lambda trigger). */
6351:160:export async function runProducerTick(deps: ProducerDeps, tickMinute: Date): Promise<ProducerTickResult> {
6352:161:  const generations = activeGenerations(deps.shardConfig, deps.now());
6353:162:  const lookback = deps.lookbackMinutes ?? 15;
6354:163:  const claimTtlMs = deps.claimTtlMs ?? 2 * 60_000;
6355:164:
6356:165:  const minutesToScan: Date[] = [];
6357:166:  for (let i = lookback; i >= 0; i--) {
6358:167:    minutesToScan.push(minuteFloor(new Date(tickMinute.getTime() - i * 60_000)));
6359:168:  }
6360:169:
6361:170:  const claimed: DispatchCommand[] = [];
6362:171:  const chasingClaimed: ChasingDispatchCommand[] = [];
6363:172:  const failed: { occurrenceId: string; tenantId: string; error: unknown }[] = [];
6364:173:  let unknownEntityType = 0;
6365:174:  let scanned = 0;
6366:175:  let partitions = 0;
6367:176:
6368:177:  // Dedup guard: the same occurrence could show up in more than one scanned minute only if
6369:178:  // materialization ever wrote it under a stale bucket, which shouldn't happen - but a
6370:179:  // Set guards against double-claiming within a single tick regardless.
6371:180:  const seen = new Set<string>();
6372:181:
6373:182:  for (const minute of minutesToScan) {
6374:183:    for (const generation of generations) {
6375:184:      const partitionKeys = gsi3PartitionsForMinute(minute, generation.shardCount);
6376:185:      partitions += partitionKeys.length;
6377:186:      for (const gsi3pk of partitionKeys) {
6378:187:        const rows = await deps.store.queryGsi3<{ PK: string; SK: string; GSI3SK: string }>({ gsi3pk });
6379:188:        // PERF-12: this used to be `for (const row of rows)`, one `get`+`transactWrite` pair
6380:189:        // processed strictly sequentially - see PRODUCER_CLAIM_CONCURRENCY's doc comment for
6381:190:        // why bounded concurrency replaces that here. `seen`/`claimed`/`failed`/
6382:191:        // `chasingClaimed`/counters are shared mutable state across concurrent callbacks, but
6383:192:        // every access happens either synchronously (no `await` in between, so the JS event
6384:193:        // loop cannot interleave two callbacks' synchronous sections) or as an atomic
6385:194:        // push/increment - never a race in practice under Node's single-threaded model.
6386:195:        await mapWithConcurrency(rows, PRODUCER_CLAIM_CONCURRENCY, async (row) => {
6387:196:          scanned += 1;
6388:197:
6389:198:          // M10 cluster 4: try the chasing shape FIRST (never throws, `undefined` on no
6390:199:          // match) - the reminder branch below is completely unchanged otherwise.
6391:200:          const chasingParsed = parseChasingGsi3Sk(row.GSI3SK);
6392:201:          if (chasingParsed) {
6393:202:            if (seen.has(chasingParsed.occurrenceId)) return;
6394:203:            seen.add(chasingParsed.occurrenceId);
6395:204:            try {
6396:205:              const outcome = await claimChasingOccurrence(
6397:206:                { store: deps.store, tableName: deps.tableName, now: deps.now, claimTtlMs, newEventId: deps.newEventId, correlationId: deps.correlationId },
6398:207:                { PK: row.PK, SK: row.SK },
6399:208:              );
6400:209:              if (outcome.kind === "CLAIMED") chasingClaimed.push(outcome.command);
6401:210:              // SKIPPED_NOT_SCHEDULED / LOST_CLAIM_RACE: not failures, same as the reminder path below.
6402:211:            } catch (err) {
6403:212:              failed.push({ occurrenceId: chasingParsed.occurrenceId, tenantId: chasingParsed.tenantId, error: err });
6404:213:            }
6405:214:            return;
6406:215:          }
6407:216:
6408:217:          let reminderParsed: { tenantId: string; occurrenceId: string };
6409:218:          try {
6410:219:            reminderParsed = parseGsi3Sk(row.GSI3SK);
6411:220:          } catch {

6414:223:            unknownEntityType += 1;

6416:225:          }

6418:227:          if (seen.has(occurrenceId)) return;
6419:228:          seen.add(occurrenceId);
6420:229:

6422:231:            const occurrence = await deps.store.get<ReminderOccurrence>({ PK: row.PK, SK: row.SK });
6423:232:            if (!occurrence || occurrence.status !== "SCHEDULED") {
6424:233:              // Already claimed/cancelled/triggered by a prior tick or race - not a failure.
6425:234:              return;
6426:235:            }
6427:236:
6428:237:            const claimExpiresAt = new Date(Date.parse(deps.now()) + claimTtlMs).toISOString();

6430:239:            const now = deps.now();
6431:240:            // Same value used for both the command's own envelope correlationId (read

6433:242:            // rule) and the outbox DomainEvent's correlationId - one business correlation

6435:244:            const correlationId = deps.correlationId();
6436:245:
6437:246:            const command: DispatchCommand = {
6438:247:              messageVersion: 1,
6439:248:              messageId: deps.newEventId(),
6440:249:              createdAt: now,
6441:250:              correlationId,
6442:251:              commandType: "reminder.dispatch.v1",
6443:252:              tenantId,
6444:253:              deduplicationKey: `${tenantId}|${occurrenceId}|${newVersion}`,

6448:257:                occurrenceVersion: newVersion,

6450:259:                itemVersion: occurrence.itemVersion,
6451:260:                policyVersion: occurrence.policyVersion,

6646:62:async function handleReconciliation(event: ReminderReconciliationEvent): Promise<void> {
6647:63:  const mode = event.mode;
6648:64:
6649:65:  const expiredClaimCandidates: ReminderOccurrence[] = [];
6650:66:  const dstCandidates: FullDstCandidate[] = [];
6651:67:
6652:68:  if (mode === "CLAIMS") {
6653:69:    // GSI6 is ALL-projected - each candidate row already IS the full ReminderOccurrence
6654:70:    // item (see ExpiredClaimCandidate's doc comment), so no extra fetch is needed.
6655:71:    // Pagination is drained (bug found by Codex implementation review: the first version
6656:72:    // only ever read page 1, silently leaving any backlog over one page unprocessed).
6657:73:    let cursor: string | undefined;

6660:76:      expiredClaimCandidates.push(...(result.items as unknown as ReminderOccurrence[]));
6661:77:      if (!result.cursor) break;
6662:78:      cursor = result.cursor;
6663:79:    }
6664:80:  }
6665:81:
6666:82:  if (mode === "DST") {

6668:84:    // trigger's schedule was computed at an ambiguous/nonexistent local time, OR whose
6669:85:    // timeZone observes DST at all (see reminder-materializer.ts - broadened per Codex
6670:86:    // implementation review: a non-ambiguous 09:00 reminder in a DST-observing zone can
6671:87:    // still need re-evaluation after an offset change, not just literally-ambiguous ones).
6672:88:    // This query finds those candidates; occurrences in a fixed-offset timeZone never
6673:89:    // appear here at all.
6674:90:    const windowStart = now();
6675:91:    const windowEnd = new Date(Date.parse(windowStart) + 7 * 24 * 60 * 60_000).toISOString();
6676:92:    let cursor: string | undefined;
6677:93:    for (let page = 0; page < MAX_PAGES; page++) {
6678:94:      const result = await candidateSource.listDstCandidates({ window: { start: windowStart, end: windowEnd }, cursor });
6679:95:      for (const light of result.items) {

6681:97:        if (!policy) continue;

6683:99:        if (!item) continue;
6684:100:        dstCandidates.push({
6685:101:          tenantId: light.tenantId,
6686:102:          itemId: light.itemId,
6687:103:          itemVersion: item.version,
6688:104:          itemDueDate: item.dueDate,
6689:105:          policy,
6690:106:        });
6691:107:      }
6692:108:      if (!result.cursor) break;
6693:109:      cursor = result.cursor;
6694:110:    }
6695:111:  }
6696:112:
6697:113:  const result = await runReconciliation({ store, tableName, now, shardConfig }, { expiredClaimCandidates, dstCandidates });

8400:12:## Research declaration (research-protocol.md, E-014)
8401:13:
8402:14:**SIM PARCIAL.** The macro-pattern (decouple scan from claim via two queues) is already
8403:15:externally researched and cited in D-299 (AWS Prescriptive Guidance, Lambda+SQS developer guide,
8404:16:SQS API reference). What's new at THIS level is a sub-decision AWS has a well-documented but
8405:17:non-obvious answer for: **SQS visibility timeout sizing relative to Lambda timeout, and its
8406:18:interaction with `maxReceiveCount`/DLQ redelivery for a handler that holds an idempotency lease**.
8407:19:This project's own `sqs-worker-queue` module already encodes one specific answer (6x, fixed,
8408:20:`maxReceiveCount=5`) as a blanket rule for the dispatch case ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â applying it unmodified to a
8409:21:lease-holding consumer needs to be checked against AWS's own guidance on visibility timeout vs.
8410:22:in-flight processing time, because a lease-based state machine changes what "redelivery mid-lease"
8411:23:means (D-299's own R3ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Â Ã¢â‚¬â„¢R4 finding). Checklist applied this round, sourced from AWS Lambda Developer
8412:24:Guide "Using Lambda with Amazon SQS" (event source mapping / partial batch response) and AWS SQS
8413:25:"Amazon SQS visibility timeout" page (both already cited as sources in D-299, re-read here for the
8414:26:consumer-timeout-vs-lease-duration angle specifically, no new source needed):
8415:27:1. Visibility timeout must exceed **worst-case** processing time, not average ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â for a lease-based
8416:28:   consumer, worst case includes lease renewal, not just one page's work.
8417:29:2. `maxReceiveCount` ÃƒÆ’Ã¢â‚¬â€ avg processing time bounds how long a poison message cycles before DLQ ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â
8418:30:   must be reconciled with lease `leaseUntil` duration so an expired lease and an SQS redelivery
8419:31:   don't race in a way that duplicates or drops work (D-299's exact concern, now at the queue-timer
8420:32:   level instead of the state-machine level).
8421:33:3. Batch size for the scan-continuation queue must stay effectively 1 (see Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â§3 below) ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â AWS's own
8422:34:   guidance warns partial-batch-failure handling gets materially harder above batch size 1 when
8423:35:   messages are causally chained (continuation N+1 must not be visible before N's page commits).
