8459:71:## 2. Page-lease state machine
8460:72:
8461:73:**Item** (main table, single-table design ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â PK/SK pattern matches existing shard-scan items in
8462:74:`dynamodb-reminder-producer-store.ts`, confirmed against that file):
8463:75:
8464:76:```
8465:77:PK: SCAN#<shardId>#<tickMinuteISO>     e.g. SCAN#3#2026-09-14T22:31:00Z
8466:78:SK: LEASE
8467:79:entityType: "ReminderScanLease"
8468:80:status: "IN_PROGRESS" | "COMPLETED"
8469:81:ownerToken: string (randomUUID, one per Lambda invocation attempt ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â NOT per SQS messageId,
8470:82:            so a redelivered SQS message that re-enters the same invocation semantics gets a
8471:83:            fresh token and must re-win the conditional acquire, closing the exact silent-drop
8472:84:            hole D-299 R3 found in the stateless-fence design)
8473:85:leaseUntil: number (epoch ms)
8474:86:lastEvaluatedKey: string | undefined (JSON-serialized DynamoDB ExclusiveStartKey for queryGsi3,
8475:87:            undefined on the first page, present on every continuation)
8476:88:pagesProcessed: number
8477:89:candidatesPublished: number
8478:90:version: number (occ.ts optimistic concurrency, same convention as every other mutable item)
8479:91:ttl: epoch seconds, 7 days after leaseUntil ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â cheap cleanup, matches this project's existing TTL
8480:92:     convention on other transient coordination items (checked against `defaultShardConfig()`'s
8481:93:     neighbors in dynamodb-reminder-producer-store.ts)
8482:94:```
8483:95:
8484:96:**Acquire** (first page of a shard/minute, or reclaim after expiry) ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â `occ.ts`'s
8485:97:`buildConditionalPut` with:
8486:98:`ConditionExpression: "attribute_not_exists(PK) OR (status = :inProgress AND leaseUntil < :now) OR status = :completedNoop"`
8487:99:ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â the third arm exists only to make a duplicate "start" message (a Scheduler retry firing the same
8488:100:shard/minute twice) a safe no-op rather than an error; it still writes nothing new when already
8489:101:`COMPLETED` (checked in application code before the Put, not relied on as a silent race ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â same
8490:102:"belt AND suspenders" pattern `runProducerTick` already uses for claim races today).
8491:103:
8492:104:**Renew** (before publishing each continuation) ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â `occ.ts`'s `buildVersionedUpdate` with
8493:105:`ConditionExpression: "ownerToken = :myToken AND version = :expectedVersion"`: sets new
8494:106:`leaseUntil`, `lastEvaluatedKey`, increments `pagesProcessed`/`candidatesPublished`, bumps
8495:107:`version`. **This update happens AFTER the claim-queue `SendMessageBatch` succeeds and BEFORE the
8496:108:continuation message is sent** ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â ordering matters: if the process dies between the batch send and
8497:109:the lease renew, the next attempt (a fresh SQS redelivery of the SAME scan message, since it never
8498:110:completed) re-reads `lastEvaluatedKey` from the STALE lease state (pre-this-page), re-queries the
8499:111:same page from `queryGsi3` (deterministic per `lastEvaluatedKey`), and re-publishes the same
8500:112:candidates. This is why **claim-queue candidates must be idempotent to redelivery independent of
8501:113:this lease** ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â already true by construction, because the claim consumer's own conditional
8502:114:`transactWrite` (Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â§ below) is the actual idempotency boundary for claiming, not the scan side. The
8503:115:lease's job is only to make forward SCAN progress resumable exactly-once-effectively, not to
8504:116:dedupe claims (that guarantee already exists one layer down).
8505:117:
8506:118:**Release** (last page, `queryGsi3` returns no `LastEvaluatedKey`) ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â `buildVersionedUpdate` sets
8507:119:`status = "COMPLETED"`, same ownerToken/version condition.
8508:120:
8509:121:**Expire**: no active "expire" write ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â a lease simply becomes reclaimable once `leaseUntil < now`,
8510:122:matched by the Acquire condition above. No separate reconciliation pass is added for this (see Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â§6
8511:123:ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â `reminder-reconciliation.ts` is untouched; lease reclaim is self-contained inside the scan path,
8512:124:triggered by the SAME continuation message that would have fired next, since EventBridge Scheduler
8513:125:fires a new tick every minute and a new tick for an ALREADY in-progress shard is the natural
8514:126:reclaim trigger ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â see Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â§7 for why this is safe rather than racy).
8515:127:
8516:128:## 3. Timeout/visibility sizing
8517:129:
8518:130:Fixed module facts (not renegotiable without a `sqs-worker-queue` module change, out of scope
8519:131:here): `visibility_timeout_seconds = consumer_timeout_seconds * 6`, `maxReceiveCount = 5` fixed.
8520:132:
8521:133:- **Scan Lambda timeout**: 30s (one `queryGsi3` page + one `SendMessageBatch` + one lease
8522:134:  renew/acquire ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â bounded work, generous margin over p99). ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Â Ã¢â‚¬â„¢ scan queue visibility timeout = 180s
8523:135:  (module-derived, 6x).
8524:136:- **Claim Lambda timeout**: 10s (unchanged from today's per-occurrence claim ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â a single `get` +
8525:137:  `transactWrite`, same cost as today's inner loop iteration). ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Â Ã¢â‚¬â„¢ claim queue visibility timeout =
8526:138:  60s (module-derived, 6x).
8527:139:- **Lease duration** (`leaseUntil - leaseAcquiredAt`): **90s** ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â set independently of the Lambda
8528:140:  timeout (it is a business-level mutual-exclusion window, not a retry mechanism) but sized against
8529:141:  it with an explicit invariant: **lease duration ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Â°Ã‚Â¥ 2x scan Lambda timeout** (30sÃƒÆ’Ã¢â‚¬â€2=60s ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Â°Ã‚Â¤ 90s),
8530:142:  giving one full retry's worth of headroom before a DIFFERENT invocation is allowed to steal the
8531:143:  lease, so a slow-but-alive attempt is never pre-empted by its own SQS-triggered retry racing in.
8532:144:  Combined with **scan visibility timeout (180s) > lease duration (90s)**, an SQS redelivery of the
8533:145:  SAME message can never arrive before the lease it would contend with has already legitimately
8534:146:  expired ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â removing the specific race D-299 R3 found (two live workers believing they both hold
8535:147:  the lease) by construction, not by luck.
8536:148:- **`maxReceiveCount=5` (fixed)** on the scan queue means a poison continuation message cycles for
8537:149:  up to 5ÃƒÆ’Ã¢â‚¬â€180s = 900s (15 min) before DLQ ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â acceptable, since EventBridge Scheduler fires a new
8538:150:  tick every 60s regardless, so a stuck shard's lease will be reclaimed by a FRESH tick's message
8539:151:  well before the poison copy DLQs; the DLQ path exists for the case where `queryGsi3` itself is
8540:152:  erroring (data/query bug), not for ordinary transient contention.
8541:153:- **Batch size**: scan queue consumer batch size = **1** (continuation messages are causally
8542:154:  chained per shard ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â processing two "next page" messages for the same shard concurrently is
8543:155:  exactly the race this design eliminates via the lease, so the event-source-mapping must not
8544:156:  create that race by delivering >1 at once). Claim queue consumer batch size = **10** (candidates
8545:157:  are independent per occurrence, matches `reminder-dispatch`'s existing batch size ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â confirmed
8546:158:  against `infra/main.tf`'s `reminder_dispatch_from_queue` event source mapping).
8547:159:- **Concurrency invariant** (D-299, now with numbers): scan queue
8548:160:  `reserved_concurrent_executions` = number of shards (`defaultShardConfig()`'s shard count,
8549:161:  confirmed = `DEFAULT_SHARD_COUNT = 4` in `src/modules/reminder/domain/shard-config.ts`) ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â one in-flight scan per shard by
8550:162:  construction (the lease already enforces this logically; the Lambda concurrency cap is defense in
8551:163:  depth, cheap to set). Claim queue `reserved_concurrent_executions` = **16** (ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Â°Ã‚Â¥ sum of scan's
8552:164:  per-page candidate fan-out ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â a page of `queryGsi3` batches up to 25 candidates per
8553:165:  `SendMessageBatch` call, ÃƒÆ’Ã¢â‚¬â€4 shards worst-case-concurrent = 100 theoretical peak sends, but claim
8554:166:  Lambda p50 is <200ms so 16 concurrent claim workers clears a 100-item burst in ~1.3s ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â matches
8555:167:  PERF-12's own 10k-in-a-minute volume target with margin, verified against PERF-12's report
8556:168:  numbers in `docs/architecture/reviews/reminder-producer-structural-fix-scoping/` round artifacts).
8557:169:
8558:170:## 4. Tracing/logging/metrics/errors/outbox/writes ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â concrete
8559:171:
8560:172:- **Correlation ID propagation**: the ORIGINAL scan tick's `randomUUID()` (today's
8561:173:  `reminder-producer-handler.ts` behavior, unchanged) is carried as an SQS `MessageAttribute`
8562:174:  named `correlationId` on EVERY message this mechanism sends ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â both the scan-continuation message
8563:175:  and every claim-candidate message in a page's `SendMessageBatch` ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â using the EXACT mechanism
8564:176:  `correlationIdFromSqsRecord()`/`outboxRecordCorrelationId` already establishes for
8565:177:  `reminder-dispatch` (same attribute name, same sender-side convention in
8566:178:  `src/runtime/aws/composition/*.ts`). The scan handler wraps ALL of its work (including
8567:179:  continuation re-entry) in `runWithContext({ correlationId }, ...)`, reading the attribute via
8568:180:  `correlationIdFromSqsRecord()` when triggered by SQS and using `randomUUID()` only on the
8569:181:  EventBridge Scheduler entry point (page 1 of a fresh tick) ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â same branch shape as today's
8570:182:  handler. The claim consumer does the same on its inbound message. Net effect: one
8571:183:  `correlationId` traces a shard/minute's entire page-by-page scan AND every claim it produced,
8572:184:  queryable end-to-end via CloudWatch Logs Insights.
8573:185:- **Logging** (`SecureLogger`, no raw `console.*`): new event names ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â
8574:186:  `"reminder-scan page complete"` (fields: `shardId`, `tickMinute`, `pageNumber`,
8575:187:  `candidatesPublished`, `hasMore`), `"reminder-scan lease acquire failed"` (fields: `shardId`,
8576:188:  `tickMinute`, `reason: "already-in-progress" | "conditional-check-failed"`),
8577:189:  `"reminder-claim occurrence claimed"` / `"reminder-claim occurrence lost race"` (fields:
8578:190:  `occurrenceId` type-discriminated per D-299's `GSI3SK` distinction, `outcome`).
8579:191:- **Metrics** (`emitMetric`, EMF, namespace `ExpirationTracker/ReminderProducer` for the scan side
8580:192:  reusing the existing namespace since it's the same Lambda, and a NEW namespace
8581:193:  `ExpirationTracker/ReminderClaimConsumer` for the new Lambda, matching the
8582:194:  per-service-namespace convention `metrics.ts` documents):
8583:195:  - `ReminderProducer`: `PagesScanned` (Count, no dimensions), `CandidatesPublishedPerPage` (Count,
8584:196:    dimension `entityType` ÃƒÂ¢Ã‹â€ Ã‹â€  {`ReminderOccurrence`,`DocumentChasingOccurrence`} ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â closed 2-value
8585:197:    union, safe per dimension-cardinality rule), `LeaseAcquireOutcome` (Count, dimension `outcome`
8586:198:    ÃƒÂ¢Ã‹â€ Ã‹â€  {`acquired`,`reclaimed`,`contended`} ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â closed 3-value union).
8587:199:  - `ReminderClaimConsumer`: `ClaimOutcome` (Count, dimension `outcome` ÃƒÂ¢Ã‹â€ Ã‹â€ 
8588:200:    {`claimed`,`lost-race`,`unknown-entity-type`} ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â closed union, same shape as today's
8589:201:    `runProducerTick` result fields), `ClaimQueueBacklogAge` ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â **not emitted by the handler**;
8590:202:    already covered natively by the module's `ApproximateAgeOfOldestMessage` CloudWatch alarm
8591:203:    (D-299 explicitly names this as native, not a custom metric ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â kept consistent here rather than
8592:204:    duplicating).
8593:205:- **Error taxonomy** (`app-error.ts`): a lease acquire race that loses is NOT an error (expected
8594:206:  contention, logged/metric'd only). A `queryGsi3` failure inside the scan page throws the SAME
8595:207:  taxonomy the current handler already uses (`ValidationError` for bad continuation payload shape,
8596:208:  unchanged AppError subclasses for downstream failures ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â no new subclass needed, confirmed by
8597:209:  reading the union in `app-error.ts`; if a future round finds a gap, add
8598:210:  `ReminderLeaseConflictError extends AppError` only if contention needs to surface as a retryable
8599:211:  error rather than a logged no-op ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â deferred as a round-2 open question, not assumed here).
8600:212:- **Outbox**: candidates and the continuation message are **NOT** written via the transactional
8601:213:  outbox pattern, and this is a deliberate deviation from AGENTS.md's "critical side-effect in the
8602:214:  same transaction as the aggregate write" rule ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â because there IS no aggregate write at scan time
8603:215:  (the scan step only reads GSI3 and writes its OWN lease item; the occurrence aggregate write only
8604:216:  happens later, in the claim consumer). The outbox pattern's applicability is at the CLAIM step:
8605:217:  the claim consumer's existing `get`+`transactWrite` (unchanged from today) is the aggregate
8606:218:  write, and it already should (today's code should be checked, not assumed ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â round 2 action item)
8607:219:  carry its resulting event via the SAME `TransactWriteItems`, exactly like `SQS_REMINDER_DISPATCH_V1`
8608:220:  today. Round 1 conclusion: **outbox governs the claimÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Â Ã¢â‚¬â„¢dispatch boundary (unchanged from today),
8609:221:  not the scanÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Â Ã¢â‚¬â„¢claim boundary (new, and necessarily a direct `SendMessageBatch`, not outbox-mediated,
8610:222:  because outbox requires a DynamoDB transaction and the scan step's transaction is the lease
8611:223:  write, which is unrelated to the individual candidates being published)**.
8612:224:- **DynamoDB writes**: lease acquire/renew/release exclusively via `occ.ts`'s
8613:225:  `buildConditionalPut`/`buildVersionedUpdate` (no raw `PutItem`/`UpdateItem`), confirmed pattern
8614:226:  match against existing shard-scan-state usage in `dynamodb-reminder-producer-store.ts`.

8639:251:## 6. `reminder-reconciliation.ts` impact
8640:252:
8641:253:**Confirmed: no change needed**, with actual reasoning (not just repeating D-299's stated
8642:254:expectation): `reminder-reconciliation.ts`'s job (per its own file, to be re-read in round 2 for a
8643:255:citation-level confirmation) is to catch occurrences stuck in `CLAIMED` past `claimExpiresAt` ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â
8644:256:that contract is entirely downstream of the claim consumer's `transactWrite`, which writes
8645:257:`claimExpiresAt` identically to today's code (D-299's own premise, unchanged by this plan since the
8646:258:claim logic itself is only relocated, not rewritten). The scan-side lease this plan adds is a
8647:259:DIFFERENT state machine on a DIFFERENT item (`SCAN#...#LEASE`, never `CLAIMED` occurrence rows) that
8648:260:reconciliation never reads today and has no reason to start reading ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â a stuck scan lease
8649:261:self-heals via the next EventBridge tick's reclaim path (Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â§2), not via reconciliation. One residual
8650:262:open question for round 2: does reconciliation's own scan of `CLAIMED` rows need its OWN
8651:263:correlation ID propagation update for consistency, even though its logic doesn't change? (Leaning
8652:264:no ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â it's not part of this mechanism's message chain ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â but flagging rather than asserting.)
8653:265:
8654:266:## 7. Migration/rollout
8655:267:
8656:268:Big-bang cutover, not staged, for a concrete reason: the scan and claim halves are not
8657:269:independently useful (a scan queue with no claim consumer just accumulates candidates; a claim
8658:270:consumer with no new-shape scan producer never receives anything) ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â there's no safe intermediate
8659:271:state to stage through, unlike, say, a dual-write migration. Sequencing:
8660:272:1. Deploy claim consumer Lambda + claim queue (inert ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â nothing publishes to it yet).
8661:273:2. Deploy scan queue (inert ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â nothing subscribes to the OLD producer's shard-loop yet, since it
8662:274:   doesn't publish to it).
8663:275:3. Deploy the MODIFIED `reminder-producer-handler.ts` (now page-based) in the SAME release as step
8664:276:   1/2's infra ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â this is the actual cutover moment; the old monolithic-per-shard loop code path is
8665:277:   deleted in this same change, not kept behind a flag (D-299 didn't ask for a flag, and a flag
8666:278:   here would mean maintaining two claim code paths against the same table, doubling the
8667:279:   concurrent-claim race surface this whole fix targets).
8668:280:4. **Occurrences already `SCHEDULED` at cutover**: confirmed safe, with reasoning ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â `SCHEDULED`
8669:281:   occurrences are discovered by `queryGsi3`, not by any in-flight queue state; the OLD mechanism's
8670:282:   only in-flight artifact at cutover is whatever's already sitting in the OLD single-invocation
8671:283:   claim loop of a tick that started before deploy (which either finishes normally before the
8672:284:   deploy completes, since Lambda in-flight invocations aren't killed by a code update, or times
8673:285:   out and is picked up fresh by the NEW scan mechanism's next tick ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â no occurrence-level state is
8674:286:   lost either way, since `SCHEDULED` occurrences are read fresh from GSI3 every tick regardless of
8675:287:   which mechanism is running).
8676:288:5. Rollback path: revert step 3's Lambda code only (keep the new queues/consumer deployed but
8677:289:   inert) ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â since GSI3 access never moved, a revert to the old handler code resumes the old
8678:290:   monolithic scan immediately with no data migration needed in either direction.

8816:===== src/shared/observability/context.ts =====
8817:1:/**
8818:2: * Request-scoped correlation context via AsyncLocalStorage (m5-observability-design.md #2).
8819:3: * runWithContext is called once per record for batch handlers (SQS, DynamoDB Streams, sweeper) -
8820:4: * never once per invocation for those - so context never leaks across records in the same batch.
8821:5: */
8822:6:import { AsyncLocalStorage } from "node:async_hooks";

8826:10:  tenantId?: string;
8827:11:  requestId?: string;
8828:12:}

8830:14:const storage = new AsyncLocalStorage<RequestContext>();
8831:15:
8832:16:export function runWithContext<T>(context: RequestContext, fn: () => T): T {
8833:17:  return storage.run(context, fn);
8834:18:}
8835:19:
8836:20:export function getContext(): RequestContext | undefined {
8837:21:  return storage.getStore();
8838:22:}

8843:27: * original business correlationId via this exact MessageAttribute name - see
8844:28: * outboxRecordCorrelationId (src/shared/outbox/outbox.ts) for the sender side of this same
8845:29: * contract. Falls back to the SQS messageId only for a message that never got the

8854:===== src/shared/observability/metrics.ts =====
8855:1:/**
8856:2: * emitMetric ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â E-018/E-021 (full-audit round2): closes the "no custom metrics/dashboard exist"
8857:3: * gap, protocol ClaudeÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Â Ã¢â‚¬ÂCodex APPROVED (3 rounds, 6,8ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Â Ã¢â‚¬â„¢7,2ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â‚¬Â Ã¢â‚¬â„¢9,2, `docs/architecture/reviews/
8858:4: * emf-metrics-dashboard-scoping/`). Writes CloudWatch Embedded Metric Format (EMF) ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â a
8859:5: * structured log line CloudWatch Logs parses into a real custom metric, no `PutMetricData` SDK
8860:6: * call, no new IAM permission (every Lambda already has `logs:PutLogEvents` via
8861:7: * `AWSLambdaBasicExecutionRole`).
8862:8: *
8863:9: * **Never call this from `src/workers/**`** ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â workers are deliberately observability-agnostic
8864:10: * (`AGENTS.md` Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â§7/E-007). Only the real Lambda handlers in `src/runtime/aws/handlers/` call
8865:11: * this, right next to the `logger.info(..., { outcome: ... })` call that already exists there.
8866:12: *
8867:13: * **Dimension discipline (E-014 external research, AWS EMF spec + this project's own
8868:14: * `logger.ts` precedent)**: `tenantId` (or any other high-cardinality value ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â a user id, a
8869:15: * request id) must NEVER be a metric dimension ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â each unique dimension combination is a
8870:16: * separately-billed custom metric, and tenant count grows without bound. `Outcome` values used
8871:17: * as dimensions here are closed, low-cardinality unions (5-9 members, enumerated at each real
8872:18: * call site) ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â safe. Per-tenant investigation is a CloudWatch Logs Insights query against the
8873:19: * structured logs (which already carry `tenantId` via `runWithContext`), never a metric
8874:20: * dimension ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â see `infra/modules/observability-dashboard/`'s log widgets.
8875:21: */
8876:22:
8877:23:export interface MetricPoint {
8878:24:  name: string;
8879:25:  value: number;
8880:26:  unit: "Count" | "Milliseconds";
8881:27:  /** Closed, low-cardinality dimension values only (an Outcome union member, a fixed
8882:28:   * destination name) ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â never a tenantId/userId/requestId. See the module doc comment above. */
8883:29:  dimensions?: Record<string, string>;
8884:30:}
8885:31:
8886:32:export interface MetricSink {
8887:33:  write(line: string): void;
8888:34:}
8889:35:
8890:36:const defaultSink: MetricSink = { write: (line: string) => console.log(line) };
8891:37:
8892:38:function buildEmfLine(namespace: string, point: MetricPoint): Record<string, unknown> {
8893:39:  const dimensionNames = Object.keys(point.dimensions ?? {});
8894:40:  return {
8895:41:    _aws: {
8896:42:      Timestamp: Date.now(),
8897:43:      CloudWatchMetrics: [
8898:44:        {
8899:45:          Namespace: namespace,
8900:46:          Dimensions: dimensionNames.length > 0 ? [dimensionNames] : [[]],
8901:47:          Metrics: [{ Name: point.name, Unit: point.unit }],
8902:48:        },
8903:49:      ],
8904:50:    },
8905:51:    ...point.dimensions,
8906:52:    [point.name]: point.value,
8907:53:  };
8908:54:}
8909:55:
8910:56:/**
8911:57: * Never throws ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â a failure to serialize/write a metric must never take down the business
8912:58: * handler calling it, same discipline `SecureLogger` already follows for logging itself.
8913:59: * `namespace` groups metrics in the CloudWatch console (e.g. `"ExpirationTracker/ReminderDispatch"`).
8914:60: */
8915:61:export function emitMetric(namespace: string, point: MetricPoint, sink: MetricSink = defaultSink): void {
8916:62:  try {
8917:63:    sink.write(JSON.stringify(buildEmfLine(namespace, point)));
8918:64:  } catch {
8919:65:    // Swallowed deliberately ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â see the doc comment above. Nothing to log here either (the
8920:66:    // logger itself could be the thing failing in a truly pathological case); this is the one
8921:67:    // place in the codebase allowed to fail completely silently, by design.
8922:68:  }
8923:69:}

9045:121:/** Monthly shard for the outbox partition, matching #5.3's `TENANT#t#OUTBOX#202608` example. */
9046:122:function monthShard(isoTimestamp: string): string {
9047:123:  return isoTimestamp.slice(0, 7).replace("-", "");
9048:124:}
9049:125:
9050:126:export function buildOutboxRecord(event: DomainEvent, destination?: OutboxDestination): OutboxRecord {
9051:127:  const shard = monthShard(event.occurredAt);
9052:128:  return {
9053:129:    PK: `TENANT#${event.tenantId}#OUTBOX#${shard}`,
9054:130:    SK: `EVENT#${event.occurredAt}#${event.eventId}`,
9055:131:    entityType: "OutboxEvent",
9056:132:    tenantId: event.tenantId,
9057:133:    eventId: event.eventId,
9058:134:    eventType: event.eventType,
9059:135:    aggregateType: event.aggregate.type,
9060:136:    aggregateId: event.aggregate.id,
9061:137:    aggregateVersion: event.aggregate.version,
9062:138:    status: "PENDING",
9063:139:    occurredAt: event.occurredAt,
9064:140:    payload: event.data,
9065:141:    publishAttempts: 0,
9066:142:    nextAttemptAt: event.occurredAt,
9067:143:    createdAt: event.occurredAt,
9068:144:    GSI6PK: "RECON#OUTBOX#PENDING",
9069:145:    GSI6SK: `${event.occurredAt}#${event.eventId}`,
9070:146:    correlationId: event.correlationId,
9071:147:    ...(destination ? { destination } : {}),
9072:148:  };
9073:149:}
9074:150:
9075:151:/**
9076:152: * m5-observability-design.md #2: correlation id a relay/sweeper should use for the record
9077:153: * being processed - read from the persisted `OutboxRecord`, never from the caller's own
9078:154: * ambient context. Falls back to `eventId` only for records persisted before M5 (missing
9079:155: * `correlationId`); this is historical-data compatibility, not a new write path.
9080:156: */
9081:157:export function outboxRecordCorrelationId(record: OutboxRecord): string {
9082:158:  return record.correlationId ?? record.eventId;
9083:159:}

9085:161:/** @deprecated kept as an alias of the shared `TransactPutEntry` (src/shared/dynamodb/occ.ts)
9086:162: * for backward compatibility with existing imports - full-audit round1/qualidade found this
9087:163: * was a duplicate, structurally-identical declaration of the same shape (same pattern as the
9088:164: * expiration-store.ts/reminder-store.ts duplication decisions-log.md E-008 already fixed).
9089:165: * Do not add fields here; add them to the shared type instead. */
9090:166:export type DynamoTransactPutEntry = TransactPutEntry;
9091:167:
9092:168:/**
9093:169: * OutboxPort.append from implementation-blueprint.md #5.1: appends the outbox Put to a
9094:170: * caller-supplied TransactWriteItems array (`tx`) rather than writing directly - the caller
9095:171: * owns the transaction and includes the aggregate's own conditional update alongside it.
9096:172: * Accepts the full `TransactWriteEntry` union (Put | Update) so callers whose transaction
9097:173: * also contains Update entries (e.g. reminder dispatch's CLAIMED->TRIGGERED transition) can
9098:174: * pass their real array directly, without an unsafe cast to satisfy a narrower Put-only type.
9099:175: */
9100:176:export function appendToTransaction(
9101:177:  tx: TransactWriteEntry[],
9102:178:  tableName: string,
9103:179:  event: DomainEvent,
9104:180:  destination?: OutboxDestination,
9105:181:): void {
9106:182:  const record = buildOutboxRecord(event, destination);
9107:183:  tx.push({
9108:184:    Put: {
9109:185:      TableName: tableName,
9110:186:      Item: { ...record },
9111:187:      ConditionExpression: "attribute_not_exists(PK) AND attribute_not_exists(SK)",
9112:188:    },
9113:189:  });
9114:190:}
9115:191:
9116:192:/** Backoff schedule for OutboxPublisher retries (#5.3 step 6: "incrementa tentativas e
9117:193: * aplica backoff"). Exponential with a cap; judgment call - blueprint doesn't pin exact values. */
9118:194:export function nextAttemptDelayMs(publishAttempts: number): number {
9119:195:  const base = 1_000;
9120:196:  const cap = 5 * 60_000;
9121:197:  return Math.min(cap, base * 2 ** publishAttempts);
9122:198:}
9123:===== src/shared/dynamodb/occ.ts =====
9124:1:/**
9125:2: * Optimistic concurrency control helper - implementation-blueprint.md #5.2 / M0 deliverable.
9126:3: *
9127:4: * M0 ships no tables/Lambdas yet (that's M1+), so this module only builds the DynamoDB
9128:5: * command *parameters* for OCC-safe writes; it does not depend on @aws-sdk/client-dynamodb
9129:6: * so it stays testable without AWS credentials/mocks. M1 wires these builders into the
9130:7: * actual DocumentClient calls once tables exist.
9131:8: */
9132:9:
9133:10:export interface EntityKey {
9134:11:  PK: string;
9135:12:  SK: string;
9136:13:}
9137:14:
9138:15:export interface VersionedUpdateInput {
9139:16:  tableName: string;
9140:17:  key: EntityKey;
9141:18:  tenantId: string;
9142:19:  expectedVersion: number;
9143:20:  /** Additional SET clauses beyond version/updatedAt, e.g. { status: "CANCELLED" }. */
9144:21:  set: Record<string, unknown>;
9145:22:  /** Attribute names to REMOVE atomically in the same conditional update - e.g. dropping
9146:23:   * GSI6PK/GSI6SK when a reconciliation-candidate pointer (M3.5) stops applying. Gap noted
9147:24:   * since M3 (occ.ts was SET-only, cancelled GSI3 pointers were left orphaned because
9148:25:   * nothing actively queried them); M3.5 needs REMOVE for real because GSI6 pointers ARE
9149:26:   * actively queried by reconciliation. */
9150:27:  remove?: string[];
9151:28:  now?: string;
9152:29:  /** Extra ConditionExpression clauses ANDed to the base condition, each with its own
9153:30:   * caller-supplied names/values (W3-06 purge worker's claim/fence conditions - e.g. checking
9154:31:   * `legalHold`/`GSI6PK`/`purgeAfter` atomically alongside the version check). Each entry's
9155:32:   * `expression` is wrapped in its own parentheses before being ANDed in, so callers never need
9156:33:   * to hand-balance parens against the base condition. Placeholder names/values MUST NOT collide
9157:34:   * with the base condition's (#version/#tenantId/#updatedAt/:expectedVersion/:tenantId/:one/:now)
9158:35:   * or with any `set`/`remove` generated key (#set<i>/:set<i>/#rem<j>) - buildVersionedUpdate
9159:36:   * throws before building an invalid ConditionExpression rather than silently overwriting one
9160:37:   * caller's placeholder with another's. */

9179:56:interface ScopeCondition {
9180:57:  namePlaceholder: string;
9181:58:  attributeName: string;

9184:61:}
9185:62:
9186:63:interface ScopedVersionedUpdateInput {
9187:64:  tableName: string;
9188:65:  key: EntityKey;
9189:66:  expectedVersion: number;
9190:67:  set: Record<string, unknown>;
9191:68:  remove?: string[];
9192:69:  now?: string;
9193:70:  extraConditions?: Array<{ expression: string; names?: Record<string, string>; values?: Record<string, unknown> }>;
9194:71:}
9195:72:
9196:73:/**
9197:74: * Private core shared by `buildVersionedUpdate()` (tenant-fenced, every ordinary business
9198:75: * entity) and `buildAccountScopedVersionedUpdate()` (D-197 fatia 3/5: WhatsApp `WebhookInbox`,
9199:76: * the first entity in this repo with no tenant at all - see
9200:77: * `docs/architecture/reviews/whatsapp-channel-scoping/webhook-inbox-purge-scoping/` for the
9201:78: * 3-round Claude<->Codex protocol, both final notes >=9.0, that decided this shape). The ONLY
9202:79: * difference between the two public builders is which attribute anchors the scope fence
9203:80: * (`tenantId` vs `accountId`) - version increment, `updatedAt`, SET/REMOVE generation,
9204:81: * `extraConditions` composition and placeholder-collision detection are a single implementation,
9205:82: * never duplicated, so the two builders can never drift apart on anything but their fence.
9206:83: */
9207:84:function buildScopedVersionedUpdate(input: ScopedVersionedUpdateInput, scope: ScopeCondition): DynamoUpdateCommandInput {
9208:85:  const now = input.now ?? new Date().toISOString();
9209:86:
9210:87:  const names: Record<string, string> = {
9211:88:    "#version": "version",
9212:89:    [scope.namePlaceholder]: scope.attributeName,
9213:90:    "#updatedAt": "updatedAt",
9214:91:  };
9215:92:  const values: Record<string, unknown> = {
9216:93:    ":expectedVersion": input.expectedVersion,
9217:94:    [scope.valuePlaceholder]: scope.value,
9218:95:    ":one": 1,
9219:96:    ":now": now,
9220:97:  };
9221:98:
9222:99:  const setClauses = ["#version = #version + :one", "#updatedAt = :now"];
9223:100:  let i = 0;
9224:101:  for (const [field, value] of Object.entries(input.set)) {
9225:102:    const nameKey = `#set${i}`;
9226:103:    const valueKey = `:set${i}`;
9227:104:    names[nameKey] = field;
9228:105:    values[valueKey] = value;
9229:106:    setClauses.push(`${nameKey} = ${valueKey}`);
9230:107:    i += 1;
9231:108:  }
9232:109:
9233:110:  const removeClauses: string[] = [];
9234:111:  let j = 0;
9235:112:  for (const field of input.remove ?? []) {
9236:113:    const nameKey = `#rem${j}`;
9237:114:    names[nameKey] = field;
9238:115:    removeClauses.push(nameKey);
9239:116:    j += 1;
9240:117:  }
9241:118:
9242:119:  const expression =
9243:120:    removeClauses.length > 0
9244:121:      ? `SET ${setClauses.join(", ")} REMOVE ${removeClauses.join(", ")}`
9245:122:      : `SET ${setClauses.join(", ")}`;
9246:123:
9247:124:  const baseConditionParts = ["attribute_exists(PK)", "attribute_exists(SK)", "#version = :expectedVersion", `${scope.namePlaceholder} = ${scope.valuePlaceholder}`];
9248:125:  for (const extra of input.extraConditions ?? []) {
9249:126:    for (const [nameKey, name] of Object.entries(extra.names ?? {})) {
9250:127:      if (nameKey in names) throw new Error(`extraConditions name placeholder collides with a reserved/generated key: ${nameKey}`);
9251:128:      names[nameKey] = name;
9252:129:    }
9253:130:    for (const [valueKey, value] of Object.entries(extra.values ?? {})) {
9254:131:      if (valueKey in values) throw new Error(`extraConditions value placeholder collides with a reserved/generated key: ${valueKey}`);
9255:132:      values[valueKey] = value;
9256:133:    }
9257:134:    baseConditionParts.push(`(${extra.expression})`);
9258:135:  }
9259:136:
9260:137:  return {
9261:138:    TableName: input.tableName,
9262:139:    Key: input.key,
9263:140:    UpdateExpression: expression,
9264:141:    ConditionExpression: baseConditionParts.join(" AND "),
9265:142:    ExpressionAttributeNames: names,
9266:143:    ExpressionAttributeValues: values,
9267:144:  };
9268:145:}
9269:146:
9270:147:/**
9271:148: * Builds an UpdateItem input enforcing implementation-blueprint.md #5.2's exact
9272:149: * ConditionExpression: attribute_exists(PK) AND attribute_exists(SK) AND
9273:150: * #version = :expectedVersion AND #tenantId = :tenantId, and increments version atomically.
9274:151: * Contractually unchanged by the account-scoped sibling below - same signature, same generated
9275:152: * expression, byte-for-byte, for every one of this repo's ~40 existing call sites.
9276:153: */
9277:154:export function buildVersionedUpdate(input: VersionedUpdateInput): DynamoUpdateCommandInput {
9278:155:  return buildScopedVersionedUpdate(input, { namePlaceholder: "#tenantId", attributeName: "tenantId", valuePlaceholder: ":tenantId", value: input.tenantId });
9279:156:}

9540:417:/** Name of the AWS SDK error thrown when any entry in a TransactWriteItems call fails its

9543:420:export const TRANSACTION_CANCELED = "TransactionCanceledException";

9545:422:export function isTransactionCanceled(err: unknown): boolean {
9546:423:  return (
9547:424:    typeof err === "object" &&
9548:425:    err !== null &&
9549:426:    "name" in err &&
9550:427:    (err as { name?: unknown }).name === TRANSACTION_CANCELED
9551:428:  );

9553:430:
9554:431:/**
9555:432: * Reads the per-item `CancellationReasons` array off a `TransactionCanceledException` (verify
9556:433: * with `isTransactionCanceled` first) - the real AWS SDK error carries one entry per transact
9557:434: * item, each with a `Code` ("None" for an item that did not cause the cancellation,
9558:435: * "ConditionalCheckFailed" for one that did). Wave B2B-5 (D-095, Codex Rodada 3 achado): a
9559:436: * `TransactWriteItems` with more than one conditioned entry must never collapse "the
9560:437: * transaction was canceled" into "MY condition specifically failed" - a caller distinguishing,
9561:438: * say, a cap-guard `Update` at index 0 from an unrelated `Put` collision at index 2 needs the
9562:439: * reason for the SPECIFIC index it cares about, not just the fact that something failed.
9563:440: * Returns `undefined` (never throws) for any error shape that doesn't carry this array - callers
9564:441: * fall back to treating the cancellation as "index unknown" rather than guessing.
9565:442: */
9566:443:export function getCancellationReasonCodes(err: unknown): string[] | undefined {
9567:444:  if (typeof err !== "object" || err === null || !("CancellationReasons" in err)) return undefined;
9568:445:  const reasons = (err as { CancellationReasons?: unknown }).CancellationReasons;
9569:446:  if (!Array.isArray(reasons)) return undefined;
9570:447:  return reasons.map((reason) => (typeof reason === "object" && reason !== null && "Code" in reason ? String((reason as { Code?: unknown }).Code) : "Unknown"));
9571:448:}

9607:1:/**
9608:2: * ReminderProducer core logic - implementation-blueprint.md Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â§9.3. Pure(ish) - takes an
9609:3: * injected `ReminderProducerStore` and clock, no AWS SDK/Lambda runtime dependency, so it
9610:4: * is directly unit/integration-testable with a fake clock and fake GSI3 index (per the
9611:5: * task's requirement to test time-sensitive logic without real wall-clock waiting).
9612:6: *
9613:7: * Steps (Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â§9.3):
9614:8: *  1. read active shard generations (current + still-active legacy, Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â§9.2's reshard runbook);
9615:9: *  2. query GSI3 across N shards of minute M AND a lookback window [M-lookback, M] (default
9616:10: *     5 minutes) - "sem lookback, 'o prÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â³ximo tick reprocessa' ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â© falso";
9617:11: *  3. per eligible occurrence, conditional SCHEDULED -> CLAIMED with a short claim
9618:12: *     `claimExpiresAt`, and emit one `reminder.dispatch.v1` command;
9619:13: *  4. partial-batch-failure handling: only failed entries are surfaced in `failed`, callers
9620:14: *     retry just those (never the whole batch);
9621:15: *  5. returns counters for `scheduler_lag_seconds`/per-shard/lookback-depth metrics (left to
9622:16: *     the Lambda handler to emit via SecureLogger/EMF - this module stays observability-agnostic).
9623:17: *
9624:18: * M10 cluster 4 (D-039/D-046/D-048): GSI3 is now a SHARED scheduler for two entity types,
9625:19: * discriminated by the SHAPE of the GSI3SK read back from the index (`...#OCCURRENCE#...` for
9626:20: * `ReminderOccurrence`, unchanged; `...#CHASING#...` for `DocumentChasingOccurrence`, new) - a
9627:21: * single `queryGsi3` call for a given shard/minute can return BOTH types mixed together, since
9628:22: * they share the same physical partition space. The reminder branch below is byte-for-byte
9629:23: * identical to before this change (same transaction shape, same command, same event) - only the
9630:24: * dispatch/routing at the top of the loop is new. An unrecognized GSI3SK shape (neither pattern
9631:25: * matches) is fail-closed: counted in `unknownEntityType` (a SEPARATE counter from `failed` -
9632:26: * an unrecognized row never has a real occurrenceId/tenantId to put there) - the Lambda handler
9633:27: * (reminder-producer-handler.ts) throws whenever it's nonzero, via `shouldAlarm()` below, so a
9634:28: * real CloudWatch alarm fires - never processed or silently skipped by omission.
9635:29: */

9653:47:   * NEXT_SESSION_PROMPT.md): `schemas/queues/reminder-dispatch.v1.json` extends
9654:48:   * `command-envelope.v1.json` via `allOf`, which already required `messageVersion`/

9677:71:export interface ProducerDeps {

9679:73:  shardConfig: ShardConfig;
9680:74:  tableName: string;
9681:75:  now: () => string;
9682:76:  /** Short claim TTL - default 2 minutes, comfortably longer than one producer tick (1 minute) but short enough that a crashed dispatch worker's claim is reclaimable quickly by reconciliation (Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â§9.5). */
9683:77:  claimTtlMs?: number;
9684:78:  /**
9685:79:   * Lookback window in minutes, inclusive of the current minute (implementation-blueprint.md
9686:80:   * Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â§9.3 example: [M-5min, M]). Default raised from 5 to 15 (PERF-12 1k load test,
9687:81:   * docs/engineering/performance/results/PERF-12-async-pipeline-1k.md): under a realistic
9688:82:   * burst (many occurrences due the same minute) the producer's 10s timeout could be
9689:83:   * exceeded for several consecutive minutes, and any occurrence still SCHEDULED once its
9690:84:   * minute aged out of a 5-minute lookback was never reconciled by any other pass (see
9691:85:   * reconciliation.ts's own file header - CLAIMS reconciliation only reverts already-CLAIMED
9692:86:   * occurrences, DST reconciliation only re-materializes missing ones; neither covers
9693:87:   * "SCHEDULED, past lookback, never claimed"). 15 minutes gives roughly 2x margin over the
9694:88:   * observed 7-minute burst-recovery window, at a bounded extra cost (shardCount ÃƒÆ’Ã¢â‚¬â€
9695:89:   * lookbackMinutes extra GSI3 partition queries per NORMAL tick, most of them empty) - a
9696:90:   * dedicated reconciliation pass for this case was considered but rejected: GSI3 query
9697:91:   * access is deliberately isolated to ONLY this worker (reminder-store.ts's own doc comment,
9698:92:   * enforced by test/integration/gsi3-isolation.test.ts and infra/main.tf's "the ONLY
9699:93:   * function granted gsi3_read" policy comment) - widening the SAME worker's own lookback,
9700:94:   * combined with the timeout raise and the parallelism below (both fix the actual cause,
9701:95:   * this is the safety net), stays inside that existing boundary instead of punching a new
9702:96:   * hole in it.

9704:98:  lookbackMinutes?: number;
9705:99:  /** Deterministic-in-tests ID generator for the durable outbox event written in the same
9706:100:   * transaction as the claim (M3.5 "DecisÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â£o central: outbox durÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¡vel" - see runProducerTick). */

9711:105:export interface ProducerTickResult {
9712:106:  claimed: DispatchCommand[];
9713:107:  /** M10 cluster 4: DocumentChasingOccurrence claims from the SAME GSI3 scan, kept in a
9714:108:   * separate array (different command shape) - never merged into `claimed`. */
9715:109:  chasingClaimed: ChasingDispatchCommand[];

9717:111:  /** GSI3SK shape matched neither the reminder nor the chasing pattern - fail-closed, never
9718:112:   * processed. Should always be 0 in practice; a nonzero count is alarm-worthy (D-039). */
9719:113:  unknownEntityType: number;
9720:114:  scanned: number;
9721:115:  minutesScanned: string[];

9724:118:
9725:119:function minuteFloor(d: Date): Date {
9726:120:  return new Date(Math.floor(d.getTime() / 60_000) * 60_000);
9727:121:}
9728:122:
9729:123:/**
9730:124: * PERF-12 1k load test finding (docs/engineering/performance/results/PERF-12-async-pipeline-1k.md):
9731:125: * this loop used to process one occurrence at a time - one `store.get` + one
9732:126: * `store.transactWrite` per occurrence, fully sequential - inside a Lambda with (at the time)
9733:127: * a 10s timeout. With ~250 occurrences concentrated in one shard/minute under a realistic
9734:128: * burst, that budget was nowhere near enough, the function was killed mid-loop repeatedly, and
9735:129: * occurrences that hadn't been claimed yet eventually aged out of the lookback window,
9736:130: * permanently stuck in SCHEDULED. Bounded concurrency here mirrors the exact pattern already
9737:131: * used for the same reason in reminder-dispatch-handler.ts (D-170) - each occurrence's own
9738:132: * `transactWrite` stays a single, independent atomic conditional claim (never merged across
9739:133: * occurrences), so parallelizing here does not touch the transactional or idempotency
9740:134: * guarantees of any individual claim, only how many claims run concurrently. A plain numeric
9741:135: * constant, not unbounded `Promise.all`, to keep the burst of concurrent DynamoDB round trips
9742:136: * per invocation predictable.
9743:137: */
9744:138:const PRODUCER_CLAIM_CONCURRENCY = 8;
9745:139:
9746:140:/**
9747:141: * Pure alarm decision, extracted so the Lambda handler's "when should this tick throw" logic
9748:142: * is unit-testable without mocking the whole handler/composition root (achado real de revisÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â£o
9749:143: * adversarial, D-039/D-046/D-048: an earlier version of this fail-closed path was silently
9750:144: * absorbed by the handler - `unknownEntityType` was counted but nothing ever read it). Two
9751:145: * independent reasons, checked in this order for a stable, deterministic message:
9752:146: * unrecognized GSI3SK shape (fail-closed, never a retry-race) first, then genuine per-occurrence
9753:147: * claim failures.
9754:148: */
9755:149:export function shouldAlarm(result: ProducerTickResult): { alarm: boolean; reason?: string } {
9756:150:  if (result.unknownEntityType > 0) {
9757:151:    return { alarm: true, reason: `reminder-producer: ${result.unknownEntityType} GSI3 row(s) matched neither the reminder nor the chasing entityType - fail-closed` };
9758:152:  }
9759:153:  if (result.failed.length > 0) {
9760:154:    return { alarm: true, reason: `reminder-producer: ${result.failed.length} occurrence(s) failed to claim` };
9761:155:  }
9762:156:  return { alarm: false };
9763:157:}

9765:159:/** Runs one producer tick for wall-clock minute `tickMinute` (already floored to the minute by the caller/Lambda trigger). */
9766:160:export async function runProducerTick(deps: ProducerDeps, tickMinute: Date): Promise<ProducerTickResult> {
9767:161:  const generations = activeGenerations(deps.shardConfig, deps.now());
9768:162:  const lookback = deps.lookbackMinutes ?? 15;
9769:163:  const claimTtlMs = deps.claimTtlMs ?? 2 * 60_000;
9770:164:
9771:165:  const minutesToScan: Date[] = [];
9772:166:  for (let i = lookback; i >= 0; i--) {
9773:167:    minutesToScan.push(minuteFloor(new Date(tickMinute.getTime() - i * 60_000)));
9774:168:  }
9775:169:
9776:170:  const claimed: DispatchCommand[] = [];
9777:171:  const chasingClaimed: ChasingDispatchCommand[] = [];
9778:172:  const failed: { occurrenceId: string; tenantId: string; error: unknown }[] = [];
9779:173:  let unknownEntityType = 0;
9780:174:  let scanned = 0;
9781:175:  let partitions = 0;
9782:176:
9783:177:  // Dedup guard: the same occurrence could show up in more than one scanned minute only if
9784:178:  // materialization ever wrote it under a stale bucket, which shouldn't happen - but a
9785:179:  // Set guards against double-claiming within a single tick regardless.
9786:180:  const seen = new Set<string>();
9787:181:
9788:182:  for (const minute of minutesToScan) {
9789:183:    for (const generation of generations) {
9790:184:      const partitionKeys = gsi3PartitionsForMinute(minute, generation.shardCount);
9791:185:      partitions += partitionKeys.length;
9792:186:      for (const gsi3pk of partitionKeys) {
9793:187:        const rows = await deps.store.queryGsi3<{ PK: string; SK: string; GSI3SK: string }>({ gsi3pk });
9794:188:        // PERF-12: this used to be `for (const row of rows)`, one `get`+`transactWrite` pair
9795:189:        // processed strictly sequentially - see PRODUCER_CLAIM_CONCURRENCY's doc comment for
9796:190:        // why bounded concurrency replaces that here. `seen`/`claimed`/`failed`/
9797:191:        // `chasingClaimed`/counters are shared mutable state across concurrent callbacks, but
9798:192:        // every access happens either synchronously (no `await` in between, so the JS event
9799:193:        // loop cannot interleave two callbacks' synchronous sections) or as an atomic
9800:194:        // push/increment - never a race in practice under Node's single-threaded model.
9801:195:        await mapWithConcurrency(rows, PRODUCER_CLAIM_CONCURRENCY, async (row) => {
9802:196:          scanned += 1;
9803:197:
9804:198:          // M10 cluster 4: try the chasing shape FIRST (never throws, `undefined` on no
9805:199:          // match) - the reminder branch below is completely unchanged otherwise.
9806:200:          const chasingParsed = parseChasingGsi3Sk(row.GSI3SK);
9807:201:          if (chasingParsed) {
9808:202:            if (seen.has(chasingParsed.occurrenceId)) return;
9809:203:            seen.add(chasingParsed.occurrenceId);
9810:204:            try {
9811:205:              const outcome = await claimChasingOccurrence(
9812:206:                { store: deps.store, tableName: deps.tableName, now: deps.now, claimTtlMs, newEventId: deps.newEventId, correlationId: deps.correlationId },
9813:207:                { PK: row.PK, SK: row.SK },
9814:208:              );
9815:209:              if (outcome.kind === "CLAIMED") chasingClaimed.push(outcome.command);
9816:210:              // SKIPPED_NOT_SCHEDULED / LOST_CLAIM_RACE: not failures, same as the reminder path below.
9817:211:            } catch (err) {
9818:212:              failed.push({ occurrenceId: chasingParsed.occurrenceId, tenantId: chasingParsed.tenantId, error: err });
9819:213:            }
9820:214:            return;
9821:215:          }
9822:216:
9823:217:          let reminderParsed: { tenantId: string; occurrenceId: string };
9824:218:          try {
9825:219:            reminderParsed = parseGsi3Sk(row.GSI3SK);
9826:220:          } catch {
9827:221:            // Fail-closed (D-039): neither pattern matched - never process a row we can't
9828:222:            // identify, never skip it silently either. Alarm-worthy, surfaced via the tick result.
9829:223:            unknownEntityType += 1;
9830:224:            return;
9831:225:          }
9832:226:          const { tenantId, occurrenceId } = reminderParsed;
9833:227:          if (seen.has(occurrenceId)) return;
9834:228:          seen.add(occurrenceId);
9835:229:
9836:230:          try {
9837:231:            const occurrence = await deps.store.get<ReminderOccurrence>({ PK: row.PK, SK: row.SK });
9838:232:            if (!occurrence || occurrence.status !== "SCHEDULED") {
9839:233:              // Already claimed/cancelled/triggered by a prior tick or race - not a failure.
9840:234:              return;
9841:235:            }
9842:236:
9843:237:            const claimExpiresAt = new Date(Date.parse(deps.now()) + claimTtlMs).toISOString();
9844:238:            const newVersion = occurrence.version + 1;
9845:239:            const now = deps.now();
9846:240:            // Same value used for both the command's own envelope correlationId (read
9847:241:            // directly from the SQS body per m5-observability-design.md #2's general SQS
9848:242:            // rule) and the outbox DomainEvent's correlationId - one business correlation
9849:243:            // per dispatch, not two independently-generated ids for the same operation.
9850:244:            const correlationId = deps.correlationId();
9851:245:
9852:246:            const command: DispatchCommand = {
9853:247:              messageVersion: 1,
9854:248:              messageId: deps.newEventId(),
9855:249:              createdAt: now,
9856:250:              correlationId,
9857:251:              commandType: "reminder.dispatch.v1",
9858:252:              tenantId,
9859:253:              deduplicationKey: `${tenantId}|${occurrenceId}|${newVersion}`,
9860:254:              data: {
9861:255:                itemId: occurrence.itemId,
9862:256:                occurrenceId,
9863:257:                occurrenceVersion: newVersion,
9864:258:                scheduledAt: occurrence.scheduledAt,
9865:259:                itemVersion: occurrence.itemVersion,
9866:260:                policyVersion: occurrence.policyVersion,
9867:261:              },
9868:262:            };
9869:263:
9870:264:            // M3.5 "DecisÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â£o central: outbox durÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¡vel": TransactWrite(claim) followed by a
9871:265:            // direct SendMessage in the handler is NOT atomic (Lambda can die between the
9872:266:            // two steps, leaving a CLAIMED occurrence with no queued command - neither the
9873:267:            // producer's own lookback window nor the daily DST reconciliation reliably
9874:268:            // covers that gap). The fix: write a durable OutboxEvent
9875:269:            // (destination=SQS_REMINDER_DISPATCH_V1) in the SAME transaction as the claim;
9876:270:            // DispatchOutboxRelay (DynamoDB Streams) publishes it to SQS, a sweeper recovers
9877:271:            // publication failures. Also set the GSI6 WORKSTATE#CLAIMED pointer so the
9878:272:            // reconciliation job can find this claim if it expires unrecovered - removed
9879:273:            // when ReminderDispatch advances to TRIGGERED or reconciliation reverts it.
9880:274:            const event: DomainEvent = {
9881:275:              specVersion: "1.0",
9882:276:              eventId: deps.newEventId(),
9883:277:              eventType: "ReminderDispatchRequested",
9884:278:              source: "expiration-tracker.reminder-producer",
9885:279:              occurredAt: now,
9886:280:              correlationId,
9887:281:              tenantId,
9888:282:              actor: { type: "SYSTEM" },
9889:283:              aggregate: { type: "ReminderOccurrence", id: occurrenceId, version: newVersion },
9890:284:              data: command as unknown as Record<string, unknown>,
9891:285:            };
9892:286:            const outboxEntries: DynamoTransactPutEntry[] = [];
9893:287:            appendToTransaction(outboxEntries, deps.tableName, event, "SQS_REMINDER_DISPATCH_V1");
9894:288:
9895:289:            await deps.store.transactWrite([
9896:290:              {
9897:291:                Update: buildVersionedUpdate({
9898:292:                  tableName: deps.tableName,
9899:293:                  key: { PK: row.PK, SK: row.SK },
9900:294:                  tenantId,
9901:295:                  expectedVersion: occurrence.version,
9902:296:                  set: {
9903:297:                    status: "CLAIMED",
9904:298:                    claimedAt: deps.now(),
9905:299:                    claimExpiresAt,
9906:300:                    GSI6PK: GSI6PK_WORKSTATE_CLAIMED,
9907:301:                    GSI6SK: buildExpiredClaimGsi6Sk(claimExpiresAt, tenantId, occurrenceId),
9908:302:                  },
9909:303:                }),
9910:304:              },
9911:305:              ...outboxEntries,
9912:306:            ]);
9913:307:
9914:308:            claimed.push(command);
9915:309:          } catch (err) {
9916:310:            if (isTransactionCanceled(err)) {
9917:311:              // Lost the claim race to a concurrent producer tick - not a failure to retry.
9918:312:              return;
9919:313:            }
9920:314:            failed.push({ occurrenceId, tenantId, error: err });
9921:315:          }
9922:316:        });
9923:317:      }
9924:318:    }
9925:319:  }
9926:320:
9927:321:  return {
9928:322:    claimed,
9929:323:    chasingClaimed,
9930:324:    failed,
9931:325:    unknownEntityType,
9932:326:    scanned,
9933:327:    minutesScanned: minutesToScan.map((d) => d.toISOString()),
9934:328:    shardPartitionsScanned: partitions,
9935:329:  };
9936:330:}

10001:2: * the 501 placeholder. Two schedules invoke the same Lambda with different `mode`

10031:32:export interface ReminderReconciliationEvent {
10032:33:  mode: "CLAIMS" | "DST";
10033:34:  scheduledTime: string;
10034:35:}
10035:36:
10036:37:/** Hard cap on pages drained per invocation - matches the design's "pÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¡gina lÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â³gica mÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¡x. 200"
10037:38: * per page with a bounded number of pages, so a pathological backlog can't make a single
10038:39: * invocation run indefinitely; anything beyond this is picked up by the NEXT scheduled
10039:40: * run (every 5 min for claims, daily for DST) rather than blocking this one. */
10040:41:const MAX_PAGES = 25;
10041:42:
10042:43:const RECONCILIATION_EVENT_SCHEMA_ID = "https://expiration-tracker/schemas/events/reminder-reconciliation-event.v1.json";
10043:44:
10044:45:export async function handler(event: unknown): Promise<void> {
10045:46:  // m5-observability-design.md #2: EventBridge Scheduler producer, no upstream request to
10046:47:  // inherit a correlationId from - new UUID per invocation.
10047:48:  await runWithContext({ correlationId: randomUUID() }, async () => {
10048:49:    // P2.1 (external audit 2026-09-11): `event` was previously typed (not runtime-validated)
10049:50:    // as `ReminderReconciliationEvent` straight off the Lambda invocation - a TS annotation
10050:51:    // enforces nothing at runtime. Same schema-registry pattern reminder-dispatch-handler.ts's
10051:52:    // `DISPATCH_COMMAND_SCHEMA_ID` already uses for its own boundary, mirrored here.
10052:53:    const { valid, errors } = defaultSchemaRegistry.validate(RECONCILIATION_EVENT_SCHEMA_ID, event);
10053:54:    if (!valid) {
10054:55:      logger.error("reminder-reconciliation schema-invalid event", { errors });
10055:56:      throw new Error("schema-invalid ReminderReconciliationEvent");
10056:57:    }
10057:58:    await handleReconciliation(event as ReminderReconciliationEvent);
10058:59:  });
10059:60:}
10060:61:
10061:62:async function handleReconciliation(event: ReminderReconciliationEvent): Promise<void> {
10062:63:  const mode = event.mode;
10063:64:
10064:65:  const expiredClaimCandidates: ReminderOccurrence[] = [];
10065:66:  const dstCandidates: FullDstCandidate[] = [];
10066:67:
10067:68:  if (mode === "CLAIMS") {
10068:69:    // GSI6 is ALL-projected - each candidate row already IS the full ReminderOccurrence
10069:70:    // item (see ExpiredClaimCandidate's doc comment), so no extra fetch is needed.
10070:71:    // Pagination is drained (bug found by Codex implementation review: the first version
10071:72:    // only ever read page 1, silently leaving any backlog over one page unprocessed).
10072:73:    let cursor: string | undefined;
10073:74:    for (let page = 0; page < MAX_PAGES; page++) {
10074:75:      const result = await candidateSource.listExpiredClaims({ before: now(), cursor });
10075:76:      expiredClaimCandidates.push(...(result.items as unknown as ReminderOccurrence[]));
10076:77:      if (!result.cursor) break;
10077:78:      cursor = result.cursor;
10078:79:    }
10079:80:  }
10080:81:
10081:82:  if (mode === "DST") {
10082:83:    // ReminderMaterializer (M3.5) writes a WORKSTATE#DST_PENDING GSI6 pointer whenever a
10083:84:    // trigger's schedule was computed at an ambiguous/nonexistent local time, OR whose
10084:85:    // timeZone observes DST at all (see reminder-materializer.ts - broadened per Codex
10085:86:    // implementation review: a non-ambiguous 09:00 reminder in a DST-observing zone can
10086:87:    // still need re-evaluation after an offset change, not just literally-ambiguous ones).
10087:88:    // This query finds those candidates; occurrences in a fixed-offset timeZone never
10088:89:    // appear here at all.
10089:90:    const windowStart = now();
10090:91:    const windowEnd = new Date(Date.parse(windowStart) + 7 * 24 * 60 * 60_000).toISOString();
10091:92:    let cursor: string | undefined;
10092:93:    for (let page = 0; page < MAX_PAGES; page++) {
10093:94:      const result = await candidateSource.listDstCandidates({ window: { start: windowStart, end: windowEnd }, cursor });
10094:95:      for (const light of result.items) {
10095:96:        const policy = await store.get<ReminderPolicy>(policyKey(light.tenantId, light.policyId));
10096:97:        if (!policy) continue;
10097:98:        const item = await store.get<{ PK: string; SK: string; dueDate: string; version: number }>(itemKey(authorizedTenantIdFromPersistedEntity(light), light.itemId));
10098:99:        if (!item) continue;
10099:100:        dstCandidates.push({
10100:101:          tenantId: light.tenantId,
10101:102:          itemId: light.itemId,
10102:103:          itemVersion: item.version,
10103:104:          itemDueDate: item.dueDate,
10104:105:          policy,
10105:106:        });
10106:107:      }
10107:108:      if (!result.cursor) break;
10108:109:      cursor = result.cursor;
10109:110:    }
10110:111:  }
10111:112:
10112:113:  const result = await runReconciliation({ store, tableName, now, shardConfig }, { expiredClaimCandidates, dstCandidates });
10113:114:  logger.info("reminder-reconciliation complete", { mode, scheduledTime: event.scheduledTime, ...result });
10114:115:}
10115:===== src/modules/reminder/domain/shard-config.ts =====
10116:1:/**
10117:2: * Versioned shard configuration - implementation-blueprint.md Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â§9.2 "Reshard versionado":
10118:3: * doubling N cannot make occurrences already materialized under the OLD generation
10119:4: * invisible. `shardFnVersion` is the generation id; the producer/reconciliation query
10120:5: * every ACTIVE generation's partitions during a reshard transition window (Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â§9.6's runbook
10121:6: * acceptance criterion), not just the newest one.
10122:7: *
10123:8: * A "generation" here is simply (shardFnVersion, shardCount) - the shard() function itself
10124:9: * (stableHash mod N) never changes, only N does, so a generation is fully described by its
10125:10: * shard count. `activeUntil` is set on a generation being retired so the producer knows
10126:11: * when it can stop double-querying it (the runbook's "atÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â© a janela de materializaÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â§ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â£o
10127:12: * antiga expirar, ~7 dias ÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â  frente no pior caso").
10128:13: */
10129:14:export interface ShardGeneration {
10130:15:  shardFnVersion: number;
10131:16:  shardCount: number;
10132:17:  /** ISO instant after which this generation no longer needs to be queried (undefined = still active/current). Set when a reshard retires this generation. */
10133:18:  retireAfter?: string;
10134:19:}
10135:20:
10136:21:export interface ShardConfig {
10137:22:  /** The generation newly materialized occurrences are written under. */
10138:23:  current: ShardGeneration;
10139:24:  /** Older generations still holding not-yet-triggered occurrences, queried in parallel by the producer until `retireAfter`. */
10140:25:  legacy: ShardGeneration[];
10141:26:}
10142:27:
10143:28:export const DEFAULT_SHARD_COUNT = 4;
10144:29:
10145:30:export function defaultShardConfig(): ShardConfig {
10146:31:  return { current: { shardFnVersion: 1, shardCount: DEFAULT_SHARD_COUNT }, legacy: [] };
10147:32:}
10148:33:
10149:34:/** Generations the producer/reconciliation must query "now" (implementation-blueprint.md
10150:35: * Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â§9.2/Ãƒâ€šÃ‚Â§9.6: reads both old and new shardFnVersion generations during a resharding
10151:36: * transition window). Excludes legacy generations whose retireAfter has passed. */
10152:37:export function activeGenerations(config: ShardConfig, now: string): ShardGeneration[] {
10153:38:  const stillActiveLegacy = config.legacy.filter((g) => !g.retireAfter || g.retireAfter > now);
10154:39:  return [config.current, ...stillActiveLegacy];
10155:40:}
10156:41:
10157:42:/**
10158:43: * Doubles shard count, starting a reshard: the current generation becomes legacy (retired
10159:44: * after `retireAfter`, default input by caller - the runbook's ~7 day worst-case
10160:45: * materialization-ahead window), and a new current generation is created with double the
10161:46: * shard count and the next `shardFnVersion`.
10162:47: */
10163:48:export function reshardDouble(config: ShardConfig, retireAfter: string): ShardConfig {
10164:49:  return {
10165:50:    current: { shardFnVersion: config.current.shardFnVersion + 1, shardCount: config.current.shardCount * 2 },
10166:51:    legacy: [...config.legacy, { ...config.current, retireAfter }],
10167:52:  };
10168:53:}

10676:266:## 7. Migration/rollout
10677:267:
10678:268:Big-bang cutover, not staged, for a concrete reason: the scan and claim halves are not
10679:269:independently useful (a scan queue with no claim consumer just accumulates candidates; a claim
10680:270:consumer with no new-shape scan producer never receives anything) ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â there's no safe intermediate
10681:271:state to stage through, unlike, say, a dual-write migration. Sequencing:
10682:272:1. Deploy claim consumer Lambda + claim queue (inert ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â nothing publishes to it yet).
10683:273:2. Deploy scan queue (inert ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â nothing subscribes to the OLD producer's shard-loop yet, since it
10684:274:   doesn't publish to it).
10685:275:3. Deploy the MODIFIED `reminder-producer-handler.ts` (now page-based) in the SAME release as step
10686:276:   1/2's infra ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â this is the actual cutover moment; the old monolithic-per-shard loop code path is
10687:277:   deleted in this same change, not kept behind a flag (D-299 didn't ask for a flag, and a flag
10688:278:   here would mean maintaining two claim code paths against the same table, doubling the
10689:279:   concurrent-claim race surface this whole fix targets).
10690:280:4. **Occurrences already `SCHEDULED` at cutover**: confirmed safe, with reasoning ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â `SCHEDULED`
10691:281:   occurrences are discovered by `queryGsi3`, not by any in-flight queue state; the OLD mechanism's
10692:282:   only in-flight artifact at cutover is whatever's already sitting in the OLD single-invocation
10693:283:   claim loop of a tick that started before deploy (which either finishes normally before the
10694:284:   deploy completes, since Lambda in-flight invocations aren't killed by a code update, or times
10695:285:   out and is picked up fresh by the NEW scan mechanism's next tick ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â no occurrence-level state is
10696:286:   lost either way, since `SCHEDULED` occurrences are read fresh from GSI3 every tick regardless of
10697:287:   which mechanism is running).
10698:288:5. Rollback path: revert step 3's Lambda code only (keep the new queues/consumer deployed but
10699:289:   inert) ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã¢â‚¬Â since GSI3 access never moved, a revert to the old handler code resumes the old
10700:290:   monolithic scan immediately with no data migration needed in either direction.

11753:20:  async queryGsi3<T extends EntityKey = Record<string, unknown> & EntityKey>(input: Gsi3QueryInput): Promise<T[]> {
11754:21:    let pageCount = 0;
11755:22:    try {
11756:23:      const items: T[] = [];
11757:24:      let exclusiveStartKey: Record<string, unknown> | undefined;
11758:25:      do {
11759:26:        const result = await this.client.send(
11760:27:          new QueryCommand({
11761:28:            TableName: this.tableName,
11762:29:            IndexName: "GSI3",
11763:30:            KeyConditionExpression: "GSI3PK = :pk",
11764:31:            ExpressionAttributeValues: { ":pk": input.gsi3pk },
11765:32:            ExclusiveStartKey: exclusiveStartKey,
11766:33:          }),
11767:34:        );
11768:35:        pageCount += 1;
11769:36:        items.push(...((result.Items ?? []) as T[]));
11770:37:        exclusiveStartKey = result.LastEvaluatedKey;
11771:38:      } while (exclusiveStartKey);
11772:39:      // Security audit trail (full-audit-round1-focused-round2-summary.md, achado real): 1
11773:40:      // evento por chamada lÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â³gica, nÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â£o por pÃƒÆ’Ã‚Â¡gina - ver

11775:42:      auditGlobalIndexAccess({ indexName: "GSI3", operation: "Query", component: "reminder-producer", pageCount, resultCount: items.length });
11776:43:      return items;
11777:44:    } catch (err) {
11778:45:      if (isAccessDeniedError(err)) {
11779:46:        auditGlobalIndexAccessDenied({ indexName: "GSI3", operation: "Query", component: "reminder-producer", awsErrorCode: "AccessDeniedException" });
11780:47:      }

11783:50:  }

11874:15:export interface VersionedUpdateInput {
11875:16:  tableName: string;
11876:17:  key: EntityKey;
11877:18:  tenantId: string;
11878:19:  expectedVersion: number;
11879:20:  /** Additional SET clauses beyond version/updatedAt, e.g. { status: "CANCELLED" }. */
11880:21:  set: Record<string, unknown>;
11881:22:  /** Attribute names to REMOVE atomically in the same conditional update - e.g. dropping
11882:23:   * GSI6PK/GSI6SK when a reconciliation-candidate pointer (M3.5) stops applying. Gap noted
11883:24:   * since M3 (occ.ts was SET-only, cancelled GSI3 pointers were left orphaned because
11884:25:   * nothing actively queried them); M3.5 needs REMOVE for real because GSI6 pointers ARE
11885:26:   * actively queried by reconciliation. */
11886:27:  remove?: string[];
11887:28:  now?: string;
11888:29:  /** Extra ConditionExpression clauses ANDed to the base condition, each with its own
11889:30:   * caller-supplied names/values (W3-06 purge worker's claim/fence conditions - e.g. checking
11890:31:   * `legalHold`/`GSI6PK`/`purgeAfter` atomically alongside the version check). Each entry's
11891:32:   * `expression` is wrapped in its own parentheses before being ANDed in, so callers never need
11892:33:   * to hand-balance parens against the base condition. Placeholder names/values MUST NOT collide
11893:34:   * with the base condition's (#version/#tenantId/#updatedAt/:expectedVersion/:tenantId/:one/:now)
11894:35:   * or with any `set`/`remove` generated key (#set<i>/:set<i>/#rem<j>) - buildVersionedUpdate
11895:36:   * throws before building an invalid ConditionExpression rather than silently overwriting one
11896:37:   * caller's placeholder with another's. */
11897:38:  extraConditions?: Array<{ expression: string; names?: Record<string, string>; values?: Record<string, unknown> }>;
11898:39:}

11915:56:interface ScopeCondition {
11916:57:  namePlaceholder: string;
11917:58:  attributeName: string;
11918:59:  valuePlaceholder: string;
11919:60:  value: string;
11920:61:}
11921:62:
11922:63:interface ScopedVersionedUpdateInput {
11923:64:  tableName: string;
11924:65:  key: EntityKey;
11925:66:  expectedVersion: number;
11926:67:  set: Record<string, unknown>;
11927:68:  remove?: string[];
11928:69:  now?: string;
11929:70:  extraConditions?: Array<{ expression: string; names?: Record<string, string>; values?: Record<string, unknown> }>;
11930:71:}
11931:72:
11932:73:/**
11933:74: * Private core shared by `buildVersionedUpdate()` (tenant-fenced, every ordinary business
11934:75: * entity) and `buildAccountScopedVersionedUpdate()` (D-197 fatia 3/5: WhatsApp `WebhookInbox`,
11935:76: * the first entity in this repo with no tenant at all - see
11936:77: * `docs/architecture/reviews/whatsapp-channel-scoping/webhook-inbox-purge-scoping/` for the
11937:78: * 3-round Claude<->Codex protocol, both final notes >=9.0, that decided this shape). The ONLY
11938:79: * difference between the two public builders is which attribute anchors the scope fence
11939:80: * (`tenantId` vs `accountId`) - version increment, `updatedAt`, SET/REMOVE generation,
11940:81: * `extraConditions` composition and placeholder-collision detection are a single implementation,
11941:82: * never duplicated, so the two builders can never drift apart on anything but their fence.
11942:83: */
11943:84:function buildScopedVersionedUpdate(input: ScopedVersionedUpdateInput, scope: ScopeCondition): DynamoUpdateCommandInput {
11944:85:  const now = input.now ?? new Date().toISOString();
11945:86:
11946:87:  const names: Record<string, string> = {
11947:88:    "#version": "version",
11948:89:    [scope.namePlaceholder]: scope.attributeName,
11949:90:    "#updatedAt": "updatedAt",
11950:91:  };
11951:92:  const values: Record<string, unknown> = {
11952:93:    ":expectedVersion": input.expectedVersion,
11953:94:    [scope.valuePlaceholder]: scope.value,
11954:95:    ":one": 1,
11955:96:    ":now": now,
11956:97:  };
11957:98:
11958:99:  const setClauses = ["#version = #version + :one", "#updatedAt = :now"];
11959:100:  let i = 0;
11960:101:  for (const [field, value] of Object.entries(input.set)) {
11961:102:    const nameKey = `#set${i}`;
11962:103:    const valueKey = `:set${i}`;
11963:104:    names[nameKey] = field;
11964:105:    values[valueKey] = value;
11965:106:    setClauses.push(`${nameKey} = ${valueKey}`);
11966:107:    i += 1;
11967:108:  }
11968:109:
11969:110:  const removeClauses: string[] = [];
11970:111:  let j = 0;
11971:112:  for (const field of input.remove ?? []) {
11972:113:    const nameKey = `#rem${j}`;
11973:114:    names[nameKey] = field;
11974:115:    removeClauses.push(nameKey);
11975:116:    j += 1;
11976:117:  }
11977:118:
11978:119:  const expression =
11979:120:    removeClauses.length > 0
11980:121:      ? `SET ${setClauses.join(", ")} REMOVE ${removeClauses.join(", ")}`
11981:122:      : `SET ${setClauses.join(", ")}`;
11982:123:
11983:124:  const baseConditionParts = ["attribute_exists(PK)", "attribute_exists(SK)", "#version = :expectedVersion", `${scope.namePlaceholder} = ${scope.valuePlaceholder}`];
11984:125:  for (const extra of input.extraConditions ?? []) {
11985:126:    for (const [nameKey, name] of Object.entries(extra.names ?? {})) {
11986:127:      if (nameKey in names) throw new Error(`extraConditions name placeholder collides with a reserved/generated key: ${nameKey}`);
11987:128:      names[nameKey] = name;
11988:129:    }
11989:130:    for (const [valueKey, value] of Object.entries(extra.values ?? {})) {
11990:131:      if (valueKey in values) throw new Error(`extraConditions value placeholder collides with a reserved/generated key: ${valueKey}`);
11991:132:      values[valueKey] = value;
11992:133:    }
11993:134:    baseConditionParts.push(`(${extra.expression})`);
11994:135:  }
11995:136:
11996:137:  return {
11997:138:    TableName: input.tableName,
11998:139:    Key: input.key,
11999:140:    UpdateExpression: expression,
12000:141:    ConditionExpression: baseConditionParts.join(" AND "),
12001:142:    ExpressionAttributeNames: names,
12002:143:    ExpressionAttributeValues: values,
12003:144:  };
12004:145:}
12005:146:
12006:147:/**
12007:148: * Builds an UpdateItem input enforcing implementation-blueprint.md #5.2's exact
12008:149: * ConditionExpression: attribute_exists(PK) AND attribute_exists(SK) AND
12009:150: * #version = :expectedVersion AND #tenantId = :tenantId, and increments version atomically.
12010:151: * Contractually unchanged by the account-scoped sibling below - same signature, same generated
12011:152: * expression, byte-for-byte, for every one of this repo's ~40 existing call sites.
12012:153: */
12013:154:export function buildVersionedUpdate(input: VersionedUpdateInput): DynamoUpdateCommandInput {
12014:155:  return buildScopedVersionedUpdate(input, { namePlaceholder: "#tenantId", attributeName: "tenantId", valuePlaceholder: ":tenantId", value: input.tenantId });
12015:156:}
